confirmed.title: The "On screen right now" heading sits 0px below the ticker card
confirmed.evidence:
.ps-ticker { overflow: hidden; border-radius: 14px; background: var(--hcard); padding: 0.45rem 0;
      box-shadow: 0 4px 14px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.28); }   /* no margin at all */
confirmed.why: This is Trym's complaint #2, and it is exact. Trace the LIVE stack: pulse-shell.js:164 appends `.ps-ticker` (zero margin), :168 appends `.ps-tnote` (hidden by default, so it contributes nothing), :172 appends `.ps-lists` — which has NO CSS rule anywhere in the codebase (grep for `ps-lists` hits only pulse-shell.js:172) — and :213 calls renderNow(lists,S), whose first act is section(into,'On screen right now'). `.hqp-sec` is `margin: 0 0 1.5rem` (inbox.astro:48, top margin ZERO) and `.hqp-h` is `margin: 0 0 0.7rem` (:49, top margin ZERO). Every box in that chain has a zero top margin, so the Archivo Black heading's cap-height lands hard on the ticker card's rounded bottom edge. The largest section break on the desk renders as no break at all.
confirmed.fix: Two lines. Give the ticker its bottom margin at inbox.astro:146 — `.ps-ticker { overflow: hidden; border-radius: 14px; background: var(--hcard); padding: 0.55rem 0; margin: 0 0 0.5rem; box-shadow: 0 4px 14px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.28); }` — and add the missing rule for the container right after `.ps-tnote` at :156: `.ps-lists { display: block; margin-top: 1.5rem; }`. 1.5rem matches `.hqp-sec`'s own bottom margin, so a section boundary in the LIVE room reads identically to one in Overview.
confirmed.fixCorrection:
The diagnosis is right and the outcome the fix aims at is right, but the fix as written is two-thirds inert and carries one undeclared change. Ship the one line that does the work.

WHY THE PROPOSED VERSION IS WRONG:
a) MARGIN COLLAPSING. `.ps-ticker` and `.ps-lists` are adjacent in-flow siblings with no border or padding between them, so a 0.5rem bottom margin and a 1.5rem top margin COLLAPSE to max(0.5, 1.5) = 1.5rem — not 2rem. The ticker's new margin contributes nothing in the default state.
b) IT CONTRIBUTES NOTHING IN THE OTHER STATE EITHER. When the explainer is open, the order is ticker → .ps-tnote → .ps-lists, and `.ps-tnote { margin: 0.5rem 0 0; ... }` (inbox.astro:155) already supplies exactly 0.5rem. Adding 0.5rem to the ticker collapses against it to the same 0.5rem the desk shows today.
c) UNDECLARED CHANGE. The rewritten rule silently changes `padding: 0.45rem 0` to `padding: 0.55rem 0`, making the ticker card ~3px taller. That is not part of the reported problem and is not mentioned in the description.
d) `display: block` on a `<div>` is a no-op.

THE CORRECTED FIX — one line, added after `.ps-tnote` at src/pages/inbox.astro:156, leaving :146-147 untouched:

    /* the biggest break in the LIVE room is a section boundary, so it gets a
       section's air — .hqp-sec's own 1.5rem, matching Overview */
    .ps-lists { margin-top: 1.5rem; }

VERIFIED SIDE EFFECTS: none. `.ps-lists` exists in exactly one place (pulse-shell.js:172) and is read by no measuring code — nothing calls getBoundingClientRect or offsetTop on it. Overview is untouched because pulse-shell.js:245 calls `renderNow(body, S)` with no `.ps-lists` wrapper, so there is no double-spacing risk; this brings LIVE up to Overview's spacing rather than adding to it. The sticky `.ps-bar` (:102) is position:sticky, so pushing content down does not disturb it.

ONE COSMETIC EDGE CASE, worth knowing but not worth guarding: before the first live payload lands, `into._live` returns at pulse-shell.js:175-176 (`const L = S.live; if (!L) return;`), so `.ps-lists` stays empty. An empty block with no border/padding self-collapses, leaving 1.5rem of invisible trailing space at the bottom of the room for a moment. Harmless. If you want it exact, use `.ps-lists:not(:empty) { margin-top: 1.5rem; }` instead — but plain `.ps-lists` is fine and cheaper to read.

confirmed.title: `.hqp-sec` has no top margin, so the first section in any container is always flush
confirmed.evidence: .hqp-sec { margin: 0 0 1.5rem; }
confirmed.why: This is the class behind Trym's "proper spacing between headers". Section-to-section spacing works only because the PREVIOUS section supplies 1.5rem of bottom margin. The moment a section is the first child of anything — `.ps-lists` (pulse-shell.js:172→213), or `body` after the `hqp-note` error line at pulse-shell.js:241, or `into` after the intraday note at pulse-rooms.js:353 — there is nothing above it to pay for the gap and the heading is flush. Fixing only the ticker leaves this trap armed for the next room anyone adds.
confirmed.fix: Replace inbox.astro:48 with two rules: `.hqp-sec { margin: 1.5rem 0; }` and `.ps-body > .hqp-sec:first-child { margin-top: 0; }`. Adjacent sibling margins collapse, so section-to-section stays 1.5rem (not 3rem), the first section in `.ps-body` keeps riding `.ps-rooms`'s 1rem, and every section nested anywhere else now brings its own top gap.

confirmed.title: The ticker text touches both side edges, and adding side padding will not fix it
confirmed.why: Trym's complaint #3. Two separate causes. (a) `padding: 0.45rem 0` gives the card zero horizontal padding — but the obvious fix is a trap: `overflow: hidden` clips at the PADDING box, so scrolling text stays visible right through any padding you add and still reaches the outer edge. Padding cannot gutter a marquee. (b) The marquee geometry is wrong. `.ps-tickin` is a shrink-to-fit inline-block of width (0.35W + T); `translateX(-100%)` therefore travels exactly that far, so the run ENDS with the text's right edge flush at x=0 — the last characters are sheared off at the left edge — and it STARTS with the text already parked 35% in rather than entering from the right, so every 26s loop visibly pops. With the quiet message (pulse-shell.js:191, ~280px of text in a ~790px desk) the whole line slides off the left and reappears in the middle of an empty bar.
confirmed.fix: At inbox.astro:146-149 replace both rules. `.ps-ticker { overflow: hidden; border-radius: 14px; background: var(--hcard); padding: 0.55rem 0; margin: 0 0 0.5rem; box-shadow: 0 4px 14px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.28); -webkit-mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0, #000 0.9rem, #000 calc(100% - 0.9rem), transparent 100%); mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0, #000 0.9rem, #000 calc(100% - 0.9rem), transparent 100%); }` — a real 0.9rem fade gutter on both ends, and it is the desk's own idiom, already used on `.ps-rooms` at :119-120. Then `.ps-tickin { display: inline-block; white-space: nowrap; padding-left: 100%; animation: ps-tick 34s linear infinite; font-size: 0.78rem; }` — 100% makes the text enter at the right edge and exit at the left with a seamless loop, and 34s keeps the old ~68px/s reading speed over the now-longer travel.

confirmed.title: The mode chips and the "grabbed the GIF" lens select are 6.4px apart
confirmed.evidence: .ps-modes { display: flex; gap: 0.4rem; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; margin: 0.6rem 0 0.4rem; }
confirmed.why: Trym's complaint #1, verbatim. `.ps-lens` (the select built at pulse-shell.js:149, whose first option is EV_LABEL.gif_download = 'grabbed the GIF') is a flex sibling of the three mode chips inside `.ps-modes`, so the only thing between a pill-shaped toggle and a pill-shaped dropdown is `gap: 0.4rem` = 6.4px. They read as one undifferentiated pill soup instead of "three toggles, then a filter". The same 0.4rem is also the row-gap, so on a 393px screen where the three chips wrap, the select lands 6.4px under them. And `margin-top: 0.6rem` is the only air between the full-bleed `.ps-mapcard` (pulse-shell.js:131, which has no margin of its own at inbox.astro:129) and this control row — 9.6px under a map.

That is 8px between chips, 16px before the select (flex gap and margin do not collapse, so 0.5 + 0.5 = 1rem), and 1rem of air below the map.
confirmed.fixCorrection:
The proposed fix does not do what it claims. I applied it verbatim to the bench and measured:

  1280 after fix: sameRowAsChips = FALSE. The select still wraps to its own line, so the promised "16px before the select (flex gap and margin do not collapse, so 0.5 + 0.5 = 1rem)" never materialises — flex gap and margin-left only add up for two items on the SAME row, and these never share one. What `.ps-modes .ps-lens { margin-left: 0.5rem }` actually does to a row-leading item is indent it: measured lens.left - chip.left = +8px, breaking the select's left alignment with the chips above it, the full-bleed `.ps-mapcard` above that, and `.ps-legend` below.

  393 after fix: document.body.scrollWidth goes 475px -> 482px. The margin-left makes the off-screen overflow WORSE.
  The only part that lands is `margin: 1rem 0 0.75rem` -> 16px of air under the map (measured airUnderMap = 16).

The correct fix is to group, not to nudge — and it must clamp the select, which the proposal never mentions. This is already in the working tree and measures clean; keep it:

  src/scripts/pulse-shell.js:143   const chipRow = el('div', 'ps-mchips', null, modes);   (chips append to chipRow, the select stays a direct child of .ps-modes)

  src/pages/inbox.astro
    .ps-modes  { display: flex; gap: 0.9rem; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center;
                 margin: var(--sp3) 0 var(--sp2); }

One thing still unaddressed by everyone: the select is 460px wide only because EV_LABEL.offer_world = 'chose Banana World from the card 🌍 (retired 27 Aug)' (src/data/pulse-events.js). `max-width: 100%` clamps the box but the option text still truncates. confirmed.title: `.hqp-note`'s negative top margin overlaps the card above it in six of its nine uses

.hqp-note { margin: -0.3rem 0 0.8rem; padding: 0.75rem 0.9rem; border-radius: 14px;
      background: rgba(244, 238, 255, 0.05); color: var(--hdim); font-size: 0.84rem; line-height: 1.45; }
confirmed.why: The -0.3rem is authored for exactly one position — directly under `.hqp-h`, where it collapses 0.7 + (-0.3) to a 0.4rem gap. It is used in nine. In four of them the note follows a card with zero bottom margin, so the collapsed margin is a bare -0.3rem and the note's translucent panel is painted 4.8px ON TOP of that card, shaving off its rounded bottom corners: pulse-rooms.js:230 (over `.hqp-bars2`), :322 and :368 (over `.hqp-funnel`), :417 (over `.hqp-tbl`, which is `overflow: hidden; border-radius: 16px`). At :54 change the shorthand to `margin: 0.75rem 0 0.8rem;` and add one adjacency rule beneath it: `.hqp-h + .hqp-note { margin-top: -0.3rem; }`. section() (hq-pulse.js:52) and renderOverview (pulse-rooms.js:118) both put the note immediately after `.hqp-h`, so both keep today's intended -0.3rem pull; the other seven get a real 0.75rem gap instead of an overlap.

confirmed.title: A caption followed by another card in the same section has a 0px gap
confirmed.evidence: .hqp-cap { color: var(--hdim); font-size: 0.76rem; margin: 0.35rem 0 0 0.2rem; }
confirmed.why: `.hqp-cap` has no bottom margin and every card class on this desk has no margin at all — `.hqp-chart` (:70), `.hqp-bars` (:77), `.hqp-funnel` (:90), `.hqp-bars2` (:205), `.hqp-analyst` (:227). So any caption followed by another component inside the same `.hqp-sec` is flush. Two live instances on the Ledger room: hq-pulse.js:256 writes the 'coins by area' caption and :258 immediately appends the 'top faucets' `.hqp-bars` card into the same section — the second chart's card edge touches the first chart's caption text. Same at hq-pulse.js:189 (caption) → :193 (`.hqp-analyst` card). The reader cannot tell which chart the caption belongs to, which is the one job a caption has.
confirmed.fix: Give the caption a bottom gap only where it sits in a section's flow, so the grid cards keep theirs. Replace :76 with `.hqp-cap { color: var(--hdim); font-size: 0.76rem; margin: 0.4rem 0 0; }` and add `.hqp-sec > .hqp-cap { margin-bottom: 1rem; }` plus `.hqp-sec > .hqp-cap:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }`. Captions inside `.hqp-analyst` and `.ps-rcard` are not `.hqp-sec` children so they are untouched.
confirmed.fixCorrection:
The core selector is right — `.hqp-sec > .hqp-cap` matches (captions ARE direct children of `.hqp-sec`), and its specificity (0,2,0) beats the base rule (0,1,0) regardless of source order, so a real gap opens above the 'top faucets' card. But the fix as written has two defects:

DEFECT 1 — SILENT REGRESSION. The proposed `margin: 0.4rem 0 0` is a 3-value shorthand, which sets margin-left to 0. The base rule is a 4-value shorthand ending in `0.2rem`. The fix therefore DROPS the 0.2rem left indent from all twelve captions on the desk, shifting every one of them 3.2px left, out of alignment with the card padding they sit beneath. Nothing in the finding asked for that.

DEFECT 2 — DEAD RULE. `.hqp-sec > .hqp-cap:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }` is a no-op. `.hqp-sec` (inbox.astro:48) is `margin: 0 0 1.5rem` with no padding, no border and auto height, and its parent `.ps-body` (inbox.astro:128, `min-height: 40vh`) creates no block formatting context. So a last child's bottom margin collapses through the parent and merges with the section's own 1.5rem: max(1rem, 1.5rem) = 1.5rem either way. The rule protects against nothing and adds a line to CSS that is already ~200 lines.

CORRECTED FIX — one added line, left indent preserved, no dead rule. Keep :76 exactly as it is and add:

    .hqp-sec > .hqp-cap:not(:last-child) { margin-bottom: 0.9rem; }

Three notes on the correction. `:not(:last-child)` is preferred over relying on margin collapsing: it states the intent, and it stays correct if `.hqp-sec` ever gains padding, a border, or a grid/flex display in a future reskin — which is a live risk on a panel that has already been reskinned twice (inbox.astro:13-17 and :27-30). 0.9rem rather than 1rem matches the existing card-to-card rhythm on this desk (`.hqp-tiles { margin: 0 0 0.9rem }`, inbox.astro:59) and stays clearly under the 1.5rem section gap, so the caption still reads as belonging inside its section. And since the only live instance is hq-pulse.js:256, this is a one-line CSS change with exactly one visible effect — every other caption is a last child and collapses as before.

confirmed.title: Captions are indented 3.2px off every other left edge on the desk

confirmed.title: The lens select renders at 16px beside 11.84px chips — the mode row is visibly ragged
confirmed.evidence: .bm-wrap input, .bm-wrap select, .bm-wrap textarea { font-size: 16px; }   /* beats .ps-lens { font-size: 0.74rem } at :142 */
confirmed.why: `.ps-lens` (:141-142) asks for 0.74rem = 11.84px. `.bm-wrap select` is specificity (0,1,1) against `.ps-lens`'s (0,1,0) and it is declared 108 lines later, so 16px wins and the author's 0.74rem never applies. The result is a dropdown whose text is 35% larger and whose box is ~2px taller than the three chips it sits beside in the same `align-items: center` flex row — the row has no common baseline, which is a large part of why the group reads as crowded even before the 0.4rem gap. The 16px itself must stay: the comment at :249 says it exists so iOS does not zoom-jump on focus.
confirmed.fix: Keep 16px, make the boxes agree. Add after :142: `.ps-modes .ps-chip, .ps-modes .ps-lens { min-height: 32px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; }` and tighten the select's padding to match its larger glyphs — `.ps-lens { ... padding: 0.2rem 0.6rem; }`. Both controls then occupy one 32px band and the row has a single optical baseline.
confirmed.fixCorrection:
Do not equalise the boxes — stop the rule reaching the lens at all, and the author's own CSS is already correct.

Replace the min-height/padding proposal with ONE line, added after .ps-lens (currently inbox.astro :166):

    /* :323's iOS guard is for the real forms; the lens is a chip, not a field */
    .bm-wrap .ps-lens { font-size: 0.74rem; }

Specificity (0,2,0) beats `.bm-wrap select` (0,1,1), so order no longer matters and the 16px iOS guard stays intact for every actual input/textarea. Equivalent alternative: scope the guard itself — `.bm-wrap input, .bm-wrap textarea, .bm-wrap select:not(.ps-lens) { font-size: 16px; }`.

Measured after the one-line fix (Chromium, real self-hosted Space Grotesk, .bm-wrap at its 820px cap, viewport 1280):
  lens font-size 11.84px, height 28.59px, width 351.2px
  chips group 391.9px + 6.4px gap + 351.2px = 749.5px < 791.2px content box
  → one row, .ps-modes height 29.36px (was 70.34px), chip-vs-lens height delta 0.77px

Why the proposed fix is not sound:
1. `min-height: 32px` on `.ps-lens` is INERT — the lens is already 34.59px (36.19px in the current tree after the concurrent padding bump to 0.35rem at :165). Only the second half, `padding: 0.2rem 0.6rem`, does any work. Together they do measure dH = 0 (both exactly 32.00px), so the pair is not useless — but it treats a symptom that does not exist as described.
2. It leaves the lens 460.2px wide and therefore still on its own line. Two boxes of equal height on two different lines buy nothing.
3. `.ps-chip` is not only the mode chip — pulse-shell.js:102 builds the window-range chips with the same class inside `.ps-range`. Scoping `min-height: 32px` to `.ps-modes .ps-chip` leaves the window chips directly above at 29.36px, so the fix trades one mismatch for a new mismatch between two adjacent chip rows.
4. `display: inline-flex` on a `<select>` computes to `flex` inside the flex parent; it renders correctly but changes nothing — a native select already centres its own text.

confirmed.title: The funnel's step boundary is only 2.4px looser than the lines inside a step
confirmed.evidence:
.hqp-funnel { display: grid; gap: 0.4rem; ... }
    .hqp-fstep { display: grid; gap: 0.25rem; }
confirmed.why: 6.4px between steps, 4px between the rows within a step. renderFunnel (pulse-rooms.js:325-343) puts up to FOUR children in one `.hqp-fstep` — `.hqp-fbar`, `.hqp-flab`, `.hqp-fdrop` (:337) and `.hqp-fwork` (:341) — so a highlighted step is a four-line block whose own lines are 4px apart, separated from the next four-line block by 6.4px. The grouping inverts: the funnel reads as one flat stack of ten lines instead of five steps, and the WORK HERE callout looks like it belongs to the step below it.
confirmed.fix: Widen the outer gap and tighten the inner one so the ratio does the grouping. At :90 `.hqp-funnel { display: grid; gap: 0.9rem; ... }` and at :92 `.hqp-fstep { display: grid; gap: 0.2rem; }`. 14.4px between steps against 3.2px within them is a 4.5:1 ratio; today's is 1.6:1.
confirmed.fixCorrection:
The fix works as written — measured 14.39px vs 3.19px, 4.51:1 — but two things it does not say, and one refinement:

(a) BLAST RADIUS. The claim frames this as a renderFunnel problem. `.hqp-funnel`/`.hqp-fstep` have FOUR call sites, and the edit hits all of them:
  - src/scripts/pulse-rooms.js:321 — renderFunnel, drawn twice in the Shop room (:355 custom, :358 official). 3-4 line steps.
  - src/scripts/pulse-rooms.js:367-388 — "The support ask" card. Top row 2 lines, the two answer rows 3 lines each (fdrop at :387).
  - src/scripts/pulse-rooms.js:439-453 — renderWorld's shop funnels. 2-line steps: bar + label, no fdrop.
  - src/scripts/hq-pulse.js:159-170 — the shared `funnel()`, called at hq-pulse.js:240. 2-line steps.
I checked each. For the 2-line variants a 14.4px outer against a 3.2px inner still groups correctly (the bar sits tight on its own label), so nothing breaks — but the change should be verified on the World room and the support card, not just the Shop room.

(b) TAP TARGETS ARE SAFE, worth stating because `.hqp-fstep` IS the click target (pulse-rooms.js:344, :377, :388; cursor set at inbox.astro:225). Grid `gap` lives outside the item box, so widening the outer gap does not shrink the target. Tightening the inner gap shrinks a 4-line step by only ~2.4px (3 gaps x 0.8px); it stays ~60px tall.

(c) REFINEMENT. Consider changing only the outer value and leaving the inner alone:
    .hqp-funnel { ... gap: 0.9rem; ... }   /* :90 */
    .hqp-fstep  { display: grid; gap: 0.25rem; }   /* :92 unchanged */
That is 14.4px against 4px = 3.6:1, already well past the ~2:1 where proximity does the grouping, and it avoids both the sub-pixel 3.19px rounding and any shrink of the click target. One line changed instead of two, and the three other call sites keep their current internal rhythm exactly. If the desk ends up wanting the tighter interior anyway, 0.2rem is fine — it renders at 3.19px and reads cleanly at 393px — but it is buying very little on top of the outer widening.

confirmed.fixCorrection:

At inbox.astro:291-292 (currently; :218-219 in the finding's numbering):

    .hqp-aname { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; font-size: 0.95rem; margin: 0 0 var(--sp2); }

Two concrete errors, one of which ships a visual regression.

ERROR 1 — the table half names classes that do not exist. `.hqp-tbl.is-grid` and `.hqp-tn` return zero matches across src/. Applied verbatim, the fix produces unstyled divs. The pattern that actually exists is `grid()` at hq-pulse.js:75-96, whose CSS is already written at inbox.astro:270-286 (.hqp-grid, .hqp-gin, .hqp-grow, .hqp-grow.is-head, .hqp-gh, .hqp-gk, .hqp-gv, .hqp-gv.is-zero), and it takes per-column widths, not a `repeat()` shorthand:

  grid(s, [
    { h: 'source',     w: 'minmax(9rem, 1fr)' },
    { h: 'medium',     w: 'minmax(5rem, auto)' },
    { h: 'sessions',   w: '5.2rem', num: true },
    { h: 'engaged',    w: '4.8rem', num: true },
    { h: 'pages each', w: '5.6rem', num: true },
  ], srcRows.map((x) => [x.source || '(direct)', x.medium || '—', nfmt(x.sessions),
    pct(x.engaged, x.sessions) + '%', x.sessions ? (x.views / x.sessions).toFixed(1) : '0']));

Note this also splits `source · medium` into two columns, which is better than the claim's plan of keeping that join in one key cell — it removes the ambiguous glyph entirely rather than leaving one of its two meanings on screen. `grid()` wraps in `.hqp-grid` with horizontal overflow (inbox.astro:270-273) and `.hqp-gin { min-width: max-content }` (274), so the 393px case scrolls sideways instead of ellipsising the label.

ERROR 2 — the funnel half does not stack; it makes a three-item row. The proposal is `div('hqp-fnum', nfmt(s.v), lab); div('hqp-fsub', pct(...) + '% of above', lab);` justified by "the funnel already stacks (`.hqp-fstep { display: grid; gap: 0.25rem }`)". But `lab` is not `.hqp-fstep`. hq-pulse.js:202 is `const lab = div('hqp-flab', null, row);` and inbox.astro:110 is `.hqp-flab { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 0.6rem; align-items: baseline; }`. Appending a second child to `lab` lands it as a THIRD flex item on the same baseline, pushed apart by space-between — name at the left, number floating in the middle, "% of above" at the right. That reads worse than the middot it replaces.

The correct parent is `row` (the `.hqp-fstep` grid), and the desk already does exactly this at pulse-rooms.js:332-340, where `div('hqp-fnum', nfmt(vals[i]), lab)` carries the bare number and the qualifier goes to `row` as `.hqp-fdrop`. So:

  hq-pulse.js:204  →  div('hqp-fnum', nfmt(s.v), lab);
                      if (i) div('hqp-fdrop', pct(s.v, steps[i - 1].v) + '% of above', row);
  pulse-rooms.js:449-450 → same shape, `row` not `lab`.

Also, do not invent `.hqp-fsub`. `.hqp-fdrop { color: var(--hdim); font-size: 0.7rem; }` (inbox.astro:300) is already the dim sub-line the fix describes, and it is already used by the download funnel. Adding a near-identical class is the "fix the instance not the class" mistake.

ERROR 3, minor — the fix says "leave hq-pulse.js:121 (a two-item tooltip) alone" while counting it among the sixteen. Drop it from the count. Likewise pulse-rooms.js:78 (a device share LIST) and hq-pulse.js:188 (a gate fallback) are joins of like things, not two unrelated statistics; leaving them is correct and they should not inflate the headline.

Scope note for whoever applies this: sources, campaigns and the downloads surfaces table were converted to `grid()` in the working tree during this audit. The remaining sites are pulse-rooms.js:127 (events), :170 (ps-devv), :237 (caption), :340 (fdrop), :450 (shop funnel), hq-pulse.js:204 (funnel), :239 (confidence), :330-331 (foot), and pulse-shell.js:297 (analyst confidence). Deleting the declaration works because the initial value of `opacity` is 1, not because a system block re-asserts it. Anyone applying the fix on the stated reasoning is trusting a rule that isn't there.

(b) BLANKET DELETION FLATTENS ONE REAL TIER. .hqp-tlab (line 83) is `color: var(--hdim); font-size: 0.72rem;` and .hqp-tsub (line 85) is `color: var(--hdim); font-size: 0.72rem;` — identical ink, identical size. THE CORRECTED FIX — take the claim's own fallback as the primary, not the alternative. Add the token next to the others at inbox.astro:21:

  line 110  .hqp-rsub  -> color: var(--hsoft); DROP `opacity: 0.75;`  (4.79:1; keeps its 0.68rem size step too)
  line 330  .hqp-foot  -> color: var(--hsoft); DROP `opacity: 0.75;`  (5.38:1 on the page ground)

confirmed.title: The funnel-drift gate treats a 5-point rate difference as a finding at n=40
confirmed.evidence: } else if (pdp >= 5 && crBase && Math.abs(cr - crBase) >= 0.05) {
confirmed.why: cr is a single day's ratio and crBase is a ratio of 7-day means, but the comparison treats crBase as a constant with no uncertainty and uses a fixed 5-point cut regardless of n. At builder_start = 40/day and a flat true rate of 8%, the standard error of one day's rate is 4.3 points, so 5 points is 1.17 sd — measured, the read fires on 14.0% of days where the handoff never changed. At made=40 that demands roughly a 9-point move instead of 5; at made=400 it correctly relaxes to about 3 points, which is where a real handoff change would actually show up.

A roll fact added the same way will never say "you lost two supporters" — it needs a real `sig` computed against a baseline.

5. THE LEVELS/FOLDS SPLIT IS BACKWARDS. `passes`, `named`, `member`, `dau/wau/mau`, `ret.*` are all same-day predicate counts (foldRoll:942-969) — LEVELS. Only `coins.earned`, `coins.spent`, `rep`, `badges`, `gear`, `shelf` are lifetime sums across passes — those are the cumulative folds. Diffing a level still gives net change so the advice is harmless, but do not call `member` cumulative.

6. `ret.c1/r1` IS NOT DAY-1 COHORT RETENTION. It is rolling retention over everyone with `age >= 1` (foldRoll:967-969) — a slow-moving stock ratio. Do not narrate it as "next-day retention is sliding". If cohort retention is what you want, the rollup does not compute it and worker-pass would need the change, not worker-pulse.

7. THE `done` GUARD IS RIGHT AND WORTH KEEPING: drop rows with `done: 0` (blankRoll:921, set to 1 at 1002) from any baseline. Note the desk already handles this cosmetically — hq-pulse.js:330 prints "rolled up in full / part-way" — but hq-pulse.js:245 filters only on `d.passes != null`, so the desk DOES average a part-way row into its dau chart. Fixing that at hq-pulse.js:245 is a separate, smaller win.

confirmed.title: Google Search Console is asked for one undifferentiated row — no query, no page, no device

With per-query rows the analyst can say the thing that actually matters — "'dancing banana gif' fell from 4.1 to 7.8, that is the query that feeds the download page" — and with per-page rows it can catch the cannibalisation the gallery is already known to risk (two of your own pages trading places for one term).

confirmed.fixCorrection:
Directionally right, wrong in five checkable places. The API shape and the quota reasoning hold — tools/gsc.py:85-95 already issues dimensioned queries against this property — but as written the patch would not work.

a. gscRange's RETURN must change, and the fix does not say so. index.js:571 is `return (d.rows && d.rows[0]) || null;`. Adding a `dims` argument without touching that hands you only the single top query and silently discards the other 24. Needs: `return dims ? (d.rows || []) : ((d.rows && d.rows[0]) || null);`

b. "Divide the baseline by 7" is wrong for position. index.js:668 already gets this right for the aggregate — `clicks: b.clicks / 7, impressions: b.impressions / 7, position: b.position` — because position is an impression-weighted average, not a sum. Followed literally, a per-query baseline of position 5.7 becomes 0.81 and every query reads as catastrophically fallen. Divide clicks and impressions only.

c. The landing site no longer exists. There is no §8 and no analyst.js:340 in the tree being audited; the search fact lives at evidence.js:372-386 and prose is generated from facts, not written inline. The query rows must be pushed as facts in buildFacts.

d. And pushing them at sig >= 2 walks into the daysRunning trap. buildFacts ignores `upTo` for anything sourced from `d.gsc` (evidence.js:373), so buildPack's three lookback runs (evidence.js:427-430) see an identical fact and stamp `daysRunning = 4` immediately. A brand-new "'dancing banana gif' fell from 4.1 to 7.8" would be born labelled "Still true from previous mornings, and I will not lead with them again" (analyst.js:122-125) and never reach `reads`. Fix the trap first — give the per-query facts a real per-day series, or exempt yesterday-only facts (search, campaign, source:*) from the lookback — otherwise the new rows are invisible in exactly the way the old number is.

e. Two data caveats the narration must respect. Per-query rows drop anonymised low-volume queries, so they will not sum to the site total the existing fact prints — do not let a sentence imply they do. And `type` defaults to web: tools/gsc.py:126-127 says in this repo's own words that most impressions are the image pack, so web-only query rows cannot explain a move driven by Google Images. Also worth separating: the impressions floor the fix proposes (30 baseline impressions) is a good instinct but should reuse the existing gates rather than invent a number — evidence.js:66-67 defines MIN_RATE_N = 40 and MIN_STEP_N = 20, and evidence.js:373 already floors the whole search fact at `d.gscBase.impressions >= 50`.

confirmed.fixCorrection:
The diagnosis is right and option 2 is right, but DROP OPTION 1 ENTIRELY — the "cheap" path is both more expensive than claimed and functionally broken, and the "weight 3" read fails under it.

(a) THE CHEAP OPTION IS NOT CHEAP. apiRange's cache TTL is 60 seconds (index.js:235, `Date.now() - hit.t < 60000`), the analyst's own cache is 30 minutes (index.js:586), and there is no cron warming anything ("Generated on demand (no cron, no storage)", index.js:415). For the apiRange('yesterday','yesterday') cache to be warm at the moment the analyst regenerates, /api/report must have been hit within the previous 60s — rare. The normal case is a full cold apiRange: one batchRunReports of five plus the dls, campaign and stepTimes runReports. That is strictly MORE GA4 quota than option 2, which costs zero extra HTTP calls.

(b) THE CHEAP OPTION WOULD SILENTLY NEVER FIRE — the opposite of "weight 3". buildFacts slices its series by `upTo` (evidence.js:151, `.slice(0, cut)`), and buildPack computes daysRunning by re-running buildFacts three times with `days.length - k` (evidence.js:427-429). A fact derived from a static yesterday-only array like `d.downloads` is IDENTICAL in all three back-runs, so `set.has(f.id)` holds every time and daysRunning lands at 4 on its very first morning (evidence.js:431-435). narrate() then filters `fresh = loud.filter((x) => x.daysRunning <= 1)` (analyst.js:109) and shapeOf() does the same (analyst.js:46), so a sig-3 wiring alarm would be classed as already-reported, excluded from the headline, and demoted to a trailing clause in the "Still true from previous mornings" line (analyst.js:121-125). The regression would go out with a whimper. This is the same trap `d.campaigns` and `d.sources` already sit in.

(c) OPTION 2 IS BETTER THAN THE CLAIM REALISES — IT NEEDS NO NEW REQUEST. apiAnalyst's batchRunReports currently holds exactly FOUR requests (index.js:591, 595, 599, 607), and the comment at index.js:606 says so: "The batch caps at FIVE requests and this is the fourth." Put the `date × pagePath × eventName` report in the free fifth slot. Zero additional HTTP calls, and it stays inside the hard cap the apiRange comment at index.js:274-276 warns about ("a sixth ... takes the entire dashboard down").

(d) SHAPE THE DATA AS A SERIES, NOT A TABLE. Fold it into an events-shaped map — e.g. `dlSurface['/banana-memes/'].shown = [8 zero-filled daily counts]` keyed the same way `events` is (index.js:636-645) — so evArr/evZ can slice it by `cut` and daysRunning works. Then a genuinely new wiring break leads once and correctly goes quiet on day two, which is the entire point of the 3 Sep refactor (evidence.js:6-11, analyst.js:19-21).

(e) THE THRESHOLDS AND THE HUMAN NAME ARE FINE. `files >= 20 && shown === 0` matches the desk's existing gate exactly (MIN_N = 20, pulse-rooms.js:19/280), and DL_NAMES (pulse-dicts.js:61-71) is importable for the label. One bonus the claim missed: the desk's own caveat that a gap "in an old window ... is just the retired once-per-visit cap" (pulse-rooms.js:271) cannot apply to the analyst, whose window is always yesterday/8 days and therefore always after the 12 Aug rewiring — so the analyst's version of this read is strictly less false-positive-prone than the table Trym already trusts.

Then read it HONESTLY as a level, not a delta: the census is a live snapshot with no history, so judge ratios (`fedToday / withAnimals`, `named / yards`, `social.visits / yards`) and say "nobody has visited anyone, ever" plainly when the social block is zero — that is the highest-value sentence the analyst could print and it needs no baseline at all. confirmed.fixCorrection:
The proposed fix is wrong work: it adds a `[[services]]` binding to worker-pulse/wrangler.toml for plumbing that already exists (worker-pulse/src/index.js:559/657/672 → evidence.js:388-410 → writer.js:166), and a service-binding sub-request carries no Origin either, so it would hit worker-rave/src/index.js:382 and 403 exactly like the current fetch does. The actual fix is one line. In worker-pulse/src/index.js:657, send the origin the gate already allows:

  const w = await fetch(WORLD_STATS, { headers: { Origin: 'https://trymstene.com' } });

(The Workers runtime does not enforce the browser forbidden-header list, so Origin is settable on an outbound fetch. Verified by curl that this exact header flips 403 → 200.) Third — the part of the finding that genuinely is unbuilt. Once `world` is non-null, widen evidence.js:392-409 to compute the ratios rather than reprint counts, using today's real numbers as the sanity check:
  - daily care rate: fedToday / withAnimals = 6 / 30 = 20%
  - two-player reach: social.visits / yards = 43 / 62
  - the progression ladder from `census.stage` = [15 plot, 42 tent, 4 cabin, 1 house] — 4 of 62 have ever got past a tent, which is the single most damning number the census holds and no code reads it

confirmed.title: The coin tape's area/faucet/refusal maps say where the economy leaks and the analyst has never seen one
confirmed.evidence: foldRoll walks every player's server-side tape: `acc.area[a] = (acc.area[a] || 0) + (+e.d || 0)` and `acc.faucet[f] = (acc.faucet[f] || 0) + (+e.d || 0)` (979-980), then `for (const [why, n] of Object.entries(log.rr || {})) acc.refuse[why] = (acc.refuse[why] || 0) + n` and `acc.unruled += log.unruled || 0` (982-983). The refusal reasons are authored at line 1528 (`const refuse = (r, why) => { r.x = 1; r.r = why; log.rr[why] = (log.rr[why] || 0) + 1; }`) and the vocabulary is fixed by the RULES table at line 1395: `src`, `max`, `day`, `deny`, `owned`, `price`, `funds`, `item`, `area`. Coins are never sent to GA4 at all, so no amount of GA4 work can reach any of this.
confirmed.why: `refuse` by reason is the game saying no, counted: `funds` means the prices are above the faucet (memory already records a 70-coin wall against a 10-coin faucet), `day` means a cap is biting real players and not just grinders, `owned`/`price` mean the stand's checkout is misbehaving. `faucet` ranks which of the ~20 named taps (RULES at 1395-1444: road, stall, shed, dish, knit, rehome, quest, window, bottle, fishing, dig, wish, weed, egg, spot, floorquest) actually pays the world, which is the tuning question behind every economy decision. And `unruled` is the flag gating RULES_STRICT — a number that is supposed to reach zero and that nobody is watching daily.
confirmed.fix: Rides along with the rollup binding from finding 1 — no extra call. In analyse(), diff `coins.earned` and `coins.spent` between the last two rollup days for a genuine daily mint/burn, and read `refuse` and `unruled` as levels with a weight-2 read when any single reason exceeds ~20 in a day, naming it in plain words ("the game refused 60 grants for 'funds' — people are trying to buy things they cannot afford"). ⚠️ CAVEAT TO ENCODE: `log.ev` is trimmed to LOG_CAP = 600 events per player (worker-pass/src/index.js:1191, 1566), so `area`/`faucet`/`refuse` are a rolling recent tape, NOT lifetime totals — they must be narrated as "recently" and must never be differenced day-over-day as if they were cumulative.
confirmed.fixCorrection:
Three changes, plus a cheaper alternative worth taking first.

(a) INVERT THE CAVEAT. It is backwards for two of the three maps. `area` and `faucet` derive from `log.ev` (worker-pass/src/index.js:975) which is LOG_CAP-trimmed at 1191/1566 — narrate those as "recently", never diff them. But `refuse` (log.rr, only ever incremented at 1528) and `unruled` (log.unruled, only ever incremented at 1469) are never trimmed or reset — they are monotonic lifetime counters. They MUST be differenced against the previous rollup day to get a day's refusals; reading them as levels against a fixed "~20 in a day" threshold latches on permanently after the lifetime total crosses it once and never clears.

(b) DO NOT PROMISE A `funds` READ. Line 1537 sets `r.r = 'funds'` and bumps `w.refused` but never calls `refuse()`, so 'funds' is absent from log.rr, from acc.refuse, and from the desk. Either drop that sentence from the finding, or first fix the miscount: route it through the same helper — `if (!fresh && walletBal(w) - r.d < 0) { refuse(r, 'funds'); w.refused = (w.refused || 0) + 1; continue; }` — and add a `refused: 0` field to blankRoll (920-930) folded in foldRoll, so the wallet-level count is available too. Until that lands, "people are trying to buy things they cannot afford" is a claim the data cannot support.

(c) CHEAPER ALTERNATIVE, NO CROSS-WORKER BINDING. The refusal reason is ALREADY in GA4: park-shops.js:537 fires `track('stand_buy_refused', { item: i, why: r })`, alongside `stand_buy_try` (492) and `stand_buy` with price (516), and `rave_coin` with a coin count at banana-rave.js:742 / banana-beach.js:1120. They are invisible only because ANALYST_EVENTS (worker-pulse/src/index.js:534-546) omits them and line 598 filters them out server-side. Adding 'stand_buy_try', 'stand_buy', 'stand_buy_refused' and 'rave_coin' to that array is a four-string edit that gives the analyst a genuine per-day, already-zero-filled, non-cumulative purchase-and-refusal signal — and it includes the funds case, which the rollup path structurally cannot deliver. It rides the existing GA4 fetch with no binding, no new call, and no cumulative-counter trap. Do this first; treat the rollup binding as the follow-on for the faucet/area ranking, which GA4 genuinely cannot answer.

(d) FIX THE FRAMING. Drop "the analyst has never seen one" as if the data were invisible — src/scripts/hq-pulse.js already charts coins by area, top faucets, refusals by reason and unnamed events on the same Pulse tab. The real finding is that the analyst cannot narrate or trend them, and that nobody is diffing `unruled` daily against the RULES_STRICT gate. Note also that the desk's own 'ready to flip' badge (hq-pulse.js:323) is broken by the same monotonic-counter problem and should be day-differenced too.

confirmed.title: The device split exists in every other room and not in the analyst's
confirmed.evidence: apiRange asks `dimensions: [{ name: 'countryId' }, { name: 'country' }, { name: 'deviceCategory' }]` with sessions/users/engagedSessions (240-243) and reduces it to `devices: [{dev, sessions, engaged}]` (line 396-401); the morning report prints it as `devLine` (index.js:464-470) and the overview tile reads it at src/scripts/pulse-rooms.js:74-78. apiAnalyst's daily request (576-579) has no `deviceCategory` dimension, so analyse() cannot split a single number by device.
confirmed.why: The site is read overwhelmingly on phones — the memory files carry a standing 85%-mobile rule and mobile viewport targets of 360/375/390px. That means a mobile-only regression (a control below the fold, a card that will not scroll, a canvas that will not draw) shows up in a site-wide average as a mild dip and gets narrated as "a quiet day". Splitting engagement by device turns the daily report into a release-regression detector: "engagement held on desktop and fell 14 points on mobile" is a deploy to look at, and the current analyst structurally cannot form that sentence.
confirmed.fix: Add `{ name: 'deviceCategory' }` as a second dimension to the daily request in apiAnalyst (index.js:576-579) — the response then arrives as date × device rows; build one `days`-shaped series per device alongside the combined one and pass them as `d.byDevice`. Feed each through the existing zed()/pct() helpers and add a read that fires only on DIVERGENCE (one device's z past 2 while the other's stays inside 1), so an ordinary day where both move together stays silent and the horoscope rule at analyst.js:11-14 is respected.
confirmed.fixCorrection:
The GOAL is right; the MECHANISM is a regression. Do not add the dimension to the daily request.

1. WHY IT BREAKS. index.js:625 is `for (const r of rows(dailyR)) dayRow[dim(r, 0)] = r;` — keyed on the DATE ALONE. With date × device rows, three rows share a date and the last one wins, so `days[i].sessions` (626-632) silently becomes ONE device's count instead of the day's total. Everything downstream reads that: baselineSessions (evidence.js:449-450), robustZ (evidence.js:178), levelShift (evidence.js:164), and the blackout alarm at evidence.js:193 `if (S === 0)` which would fire on a day tablet simply sent no row.

2. THE HAZARD THE FIX NEVER MENTIONS. `engagementRate` (index.js:593) is a RATIO metric — GA4 computes it per row, so per-device rates cannot be summed or averaged back into the site rate. evidence.js:205-218 reads `today.eng` and `median(baseE)` as the site-wide rate. Recombining needs session weighting, which apiRange does at index.js:381-383 but apiAnalyst does not. Any per-device request must ask `engagedSessions` (a COUNT) and divide, exactly as the range reducer does at index.js:395.

3. USE THE FREE FIFTH SLOT. index.js:606 states "The batch caps at FIVE requests and this is the fourth", and the batch at 589-612 holds exactly four (dailyR, evR, campR, srcR). Add a fifth, leaving request #1 byte-identical so every existing fact keeps its current value:

      { dateRanges: window8, dimensions: [{ name: 'date' }, { name: 'deviceCategory' }],
        metrics: [{ name: 'sessions' }, { name: 'engagedSessions' }], limit: 60 },

Zero-fill it with the existing `order`/`idx` pattern (index.js:620-623, 638-645) — GA4 omits all-zero rows per device too — and pass it as `d.byDevice`. Cost: no extra request, cached 30 min per day (index.js:585-586, 692).

4. `zed()` DOES NOT EXIST. evidence.js exports `robustZ` (line 40), `pct` (47), `rate` (48).

5. THE FACT, so the horoscope rule actually holds. Build it in evidence.js as `id: 'device:' + name`, `area: 'quality'`, and leave it OUT of CORE (evidence.js:82-83) — CORE facts survive at sig 0 (evidence.js:465-466) and would add a silent row to every pack. As a non-CORE quality fact it is dropped unless `sig > 0`, so an ordinary day where both devices move together vanishes entirely. Set sig 2 only on DIVERGENCE: one device's |z| >= Z_LOUD (2.4, evidence.js:68) while the other stays under Z_WORTH (1.8) — and gate it on that device having >= MIN_RATE_N (40, evidence.js:66) sessions. The split makes each denominator a fraction of the day's, so the honesty gate matters MORE here, not less.

6. SLICE THE DEVICE SERIES BY `upTo`. buildPack (evidence.js:421-435) re-runs buildFacts three times to compute daysRunning, and evArr/evUArr honour the cut with `.slice(0, cut)` (evidence.js:151-152). A device series that ignores `cut` reads as fresh every morning — reintroducing exactly the repetition this file was written to kill.

7. NOTHING ELSE BREAKS. analyse(d) (analyst.js:239) reads named keys off `d`, so `byDevice` is purely additive. writer.js:116-125 `allowedNumbers` walks the pack at any depth, so nested per-device figures become sayable automatically. iconFor (analyst.js:226-232) already maps area 'quality' to 🔥/💤.

8. Cite the horoscope rule as analyst.js:23-25, not 11-14 (that range is the "He was right, for two separate reasons" preamble).

confirmed.title: Funnel step TIMES are queried for the desk and never for the analyst
confirmed.evidence: apiRange runs a dedicated report for `metrics: [{ name: 'averageCustomEvent:secs_since_prev' }]` across twelve funnel events — `builder_boot, builder_start, product_tile_click, sticker_pdp_view, sticker_pdp_checkout, checkout_redirect, shop_view, select_item, view_item, begin_checkout, offer_shown, offer_click` (index.js:308-326) — and stores them as `stepTimes`. The funnel renders them at src/scripts/pulse-rooms.js:336-338 as "⌀ 4m 12s to get here". The analyst's funnel section (analyst.js:251-279) reads only counts: `made`, `pdp`, `co`.
confirmed.why: A conversion step has two failure modes and counts only show one. "18% reach the product page" is a different problem from "18% reach the product page and it takes them four minutes": the first is a persuasion problem, the second is a findability problem, and they get opposite fixes. Time-to-step is also the earliest warning of a slow or half-broken page — it degrades before the count does. The analyst already has an instinct for this (the dwell tension read at analyst.js:239-247 fires on campaign dwell) but has no per-step time to apply it to.
confirmed.fix: Lift the stepTimes runReport (index.js:308-326) into apiAnalyst with `dateRanges: window8` and a `date` dimension, giving a per-step daily series that evZ() can judge. Then add a read to §4 when a step's average time moves more than ~50% against its own week while the count holds steady. Keep the existing swallow-on-error try/catch verbatim — the custom metric may still be unregistered in GA4 admin (the comment at line 325 says so), and a missing metric must never take the analyst down.
confirmed.fixCorrection:
The direction is right; the fix as written has four defects, two of which would ship a silently wrong number.

(a) "LIFT" MUST MEAN ADD, NOT MOVE. apiRange (index.js:231) and apiAnalyst (index.js:574) are separate endpoints behind separate routes (/api/range at index.js:745, /api/analyst at :735) with separate rspCache entries. Moving the report out of apiRange deletes the desk's own "· ⌀ 4m 12s to get here" line (pulse-rooms.js:338-340). Leave index.js:308-325 exactly where it is and add a second, differently-scoped call inside apiAnalyst.

(b) `limit: 20` MUST GO UP. Adding a `date` dimension turns 12 rows into up to 12 × 8 = 96. Copied verbatim, the call truncates at 20 and bends the series with no error — the same trap the file already documents at index.js:277-279 for the date × page × event report ("a truncated tail would silently bend the daily bars", which is why that one carries `limit: 20000`). Use a limit well above 96.

(c) DO NOT ZERO-FILL THE TIME SERIES. apiAnalyst deliberately zero-fills counts (index.js:634-644: "a day with no rows must read 0, not vanish"). That rule is correct for counts and wrong for an average. A day with no builder_start rows means NO DATA, not "0 seconds to get here"; zero-filling would print a fabricated collapse and drag any z toward a fake alarm. Carry the step-time series as nulls and hand robustZ only the days that exist — and refuse to speak below a day count, the way MIN_STEP_N (evidence.js:67) already gates the funnel.

(d) `evZ()` CANNOT JUDGE IT AS-IS. evZ (evidence.js:156) is hard-bound to count arrays via evArr → `(d.events || {})[n]`. A step-time series needs its own accessor over a new `d.stepSecs` field calling robustZ directly; passing seconds through evZ silently reads `d.events['builder_start']` instead.

Two substantive amendments beyond the mechanics:

(e) SITE IT IN evidence.js, NOT analyst.js §4. That section no longer exists — push it as a fact in the funnel block at evidence.js:277-306 with an id (e.g. 'funnel:slow'), label, because and sig, so daysRunning and the "ongoing findings never get the headline again" rule (analyst.js:115-124) apply to it. A read pushed outside the fact pack would repeat itself every morning — the exact complaint the 3 Sep refactor exists to fix.

(f) KEEP THE "COUNT HOLDS STEADY" GUARD, AND HEDGE THE WORDING. banana-pulse.md names the limitation: the metric "averages the CONVERTERS' time only — survivors, not the dropped." If a slow page makes people leave, the survivors' average can stay flat while the step degrades, and it can also move for purely compositional reasons (an ad sending impulse traffic). The proposed pairing with a steady count is the right guard and must stay. Also note `purchase` is absent from the twelve events (index.js:315-317), so the analyst's last funnel step (checkout_redirect → purchase, evidence.js:278-279) can never carry a time — the rule must not claim to cover it.

Keeping the try/catch verbatim is correct and important for a different reason than stated: apiAnalyst's batch currently holds four requests against GA4's hard cap of five (index.js:604-606), so it would physically fit as a fifth — but a rejected custom metric inside batchRunReports 400s the whole batch and takes the entire analyst down. Its own runReport with its own catch is the only safe shape.

confirmed.title: offer_skip and the purchase series are the missing halves of two reads the analyst already writes
confirmed.evidence: DL_EVENTS includes `offer_skip` (line 15) and the downloads room counts it as "no-thanks" (src/scripts/pulse-rooms.js:197, 207); FUNNELS[2] names it "Just took the file" (src/data/pulse-dicts.js:58-59). "200 shown, 0 coffee" reads as a copy failure at weight 3 — but "200 shown, 4 coffee, 196 no-thanks" is a healthy funnel with a working ask, while "200 shown, 0 coffee, 0 no-thanks" means the card appeared and nobody could interact with it, which is a BUG and currently gets narrated as bad copy. Separately, either read the `purchase` series with evZ() in §6 or drop it from ANALYST_EVENTS — fetching a series every morning and never looking at it is the same silence either way.

confirmed.title: The analyst's entire lifetime vocabulary is 19 sentences, 9 recommendations and 5 paragraphs — and only 14 of them are reachable at Trym's traffic
confirmed.why: That is the hard ceiling on how non-repetitive the report can ever feel, and it is far lower in practice. Simulated over 3000 realistic days: at 42 sessions/day only 14 distinct read sentences and 13 distinct headlines are ever reachable, and FOUR whole-report shapes cover 80% of days. At 120 sessions/day it is 15 read sentences and 10 headlines. Across every scenario I could construct — organic, ad flight, level rise, level drop, 900/day — the file emitted 55 distinct read sentences in total. Reading it daily for a month, Trym sees the same dozen sentences roughly three times each with different digits. No amount of number variation reads as a new thought once you have seen the sentence before.
confirmed.fix: Stop treating prose as a lookup table. The 19 templates should become ~19 FACT DEFINITIONS in the pack (id, value, baseline, z, n, gate) with no prose attached at all, and the writing should happen once, downstream, over whichever facts survived that day. The same 19 facts in different combinations and different orders generate genuinely different paragraphs; 19 hard-coded sentences cannot.
confirmed.fixCorrection:
The fix is sound — it is, almost exactly, what HEAD already ships — but two parts of it need correcting.

1. "no prose attached at all" would break the fallback. HEAD's `fact()` at worker-pulse/src/evidence.js:85-97 deliberately KEEPS prose: line 95 `say: o.say || null`, and 17 `say:` templates survive in evidence.js (lines 170, 186, 197, 214, 229, 247, 269, 285, 301, 322, 339, 354, 364, 381, 396, 405). That is not an oversight. worker-pulse/src/index.js:677-681 states the constraint: "THE DETERMINISTIC ONE IS ALWAYS COMPUTED FIRST and is what ships if the writer is off, unreachable, slow or caught inventing a number," and index.js:682 gates the writer behind `if (pack && env.ANTHROPIC_KEY)`. analyst.js:95-98 says the same: "This is what he reads when there is no writer key set ... It has to stand on its own." Strip `say` from the pack and every no-key and every failed-validation morning renders an empty report. The correct form of the fix is: facts carry prose as a FALLBACK, and the judgement is written downstream over the pack — which is what shipped.

2. The diagnosis under-attributes. The claim pins all repetition on prose-as-lookup-table. Roughly half of it was a GATE bug. analyst.js:13-17 names it: "THE LEVEL CHECK FIRED ALMOST EVERY DAY and carried the top weight, so the report literally opened with 'The site has moved to a different level' every morning. The test compared two short windows at 35% on a site whose daily traffic swings by more than that on its own." The repair is evidence.js:99-129 `levelShift()`, now a three-part test (separation in units of its own noise, absolute floor, and it must have held). A pure fact/prose split, without that, would have produced freshly-worded prose about the same false level change every day. The second half of the repair is `daysRunning` — evidence.js:425-434 re-runs `buildFacts` at `days.length - k` for k=1..3 to age each fact, and analyst.js:115-124 turns that into "ONGOING FINDINGS GET ONE CLAUSE, NEVER THE HEADLINE." analyst.js:19-21 is explicit that this, not the prose split, is the load-bearing rule: "NOTHING KNEW WHAT IT HAD ALREADY SAID ... That one rule is what stops the report repeating itself."

3. One thing the claim did not ask for but the shipped fix added, worth keeping: `shapeOf()` at analyst.js:40-54 makes a level morning, a money morning and a quiet morning structurally different documents (analyst.js:27-29), and analyst.js:60-93 `crossFacts()` emits the only sentences that are not a restatement of a single row. Combining facts in different orders, as the claim proposes, does not by itself produce cross-facts; those have to be authored.

confirmed.title: On a notable day the headline is a substring of the first read, so the reader reads the same clause twice in one card
confirmed.why: The headline adds no information — it is the opening clause of a sentence printed again a few lines below, because pulse-shell.js:284 renders the headline and pulse-shell.js:286-290 then renders every read including the one it was cut from. Simulated, this produces headlines like 'GIF downloads up sharply to #.' followed immediately by 'GIF downloads up sharply to #. That is the awareness channel moving...'. Echoing yourself inside a 200-word card is the strongest possible cue that a machine assembled it, and it reinforces the sense that there is less here than there looks.
confirmed.fix: A headline should be a JUDGEMENT the body then supports, never a truncation of it — 'The ad is buying the wrong people' over 'Traffic up 40%'. If a written headline is out of reach for a rule engine, at minimum drop the source read from `kept` once it has been promoted to the headline (filter loud[0] out of reads.slice(0,5) at line 374), so the same words appear once. Under the LLM writer, make headline-must-not-restate-a-read an explicit prompt rule and check it by n-gram overlap before publishing.

confirmed.title: DESIGN DECISION: more rules cannot fix this — the interesting content is in the pairs, and the pairs do not fit in a file
confirmed.why: The obvious next move is to write more checks, and it is a trap worth naming before anyone spends a week on it. To get thirty non-repeating mornings you need roughly 150 templates, and the sentences worth reading are not the single-fact ones — they are the joins, of which 19 facts admit 171 pairs and 969 triples, each needing hand-authored prose and its own threshold. Every rule added also raises the chance of two rules narrating the same underlying event in different words in the same card. And no quantity of rules buys the sentence Trym most wants ('this is the third flat day running'), because that needs memory, not more branches. Rules are the right tool for DECIDING what is significant and the wrong tool for SAYING it.
confirmed.fix: Split the two jobs cleanly. Keep analyst.js as the statistician — it already does the hard, correct part (the regime check at 107-110, the sd floor at 31, the zero-day guard at 147, the eight-generated-dates fix, the sample gates) and that logic should not move. Strip every string literal out of it and have it return a pack of typed facts instead of prose. Then a writer turns the pack into English. Rank the alternatives honestly: (c) memory alone is cheap and necessary but adds no sentences, only precision; (d) variable shape alone reorders the same 19 sentences and improves feel without adding information; (a) more rules is unmaintainable and still cannot say 'third day running'. The recommendation is (b) as the writer, with (c) as its input and (d) falling out of it for free.
confirmed.fixCorrection:
The fix is sound as a whole and has already shipped, but one clause of it is wrong and the implementation was right to ignore it.

"Strip every string literal out of it and have it return a pack of typed facts instead of prose" — do NOT do this. evidence.js still authors 17 `say:` prose strings (lines 170, 186, 197, 214, 229, 247, 269, 285, 301, 322, 339, 354, 364, 381, 396, 405, plus the passthrough at 95), and analyst.js still holds narrate() and crossFacts(). That is deliberate and load-bearing for two reasons the finding did not account for:

1. THE FALLBACK MUST STAND ALONE. analyst.js:96-98: "This is what he reads when there is no writer key set, and it is also the fallback whenever the writer is unreachable or invents a number. It has to stand on its own." index.js:682 only calls the writer `if (pack && env.ANTHROPIC_KEY)`. A pure typed-fact pack with no prose leaves the no-key and writer-down paths with nothing to render.

2. THE GROUNDING RULE NEEDS THE NUMBERS PRECOMPUTED. writer.js:17-21: "THE GROUNDING RULE, and it is absolute: THE MODEL MAY NOT DO ARITHMETIC. Every number that may appear in the report is precomputed into the pack, and anything it writes that is not in the pack fails validation and the whole report is thrown away." The `say` strings are how the pack carries the sanctioned numbers into validation range.

So the correct statement of the fix is: split evidence (deterministic facts + significance + daysRunning) from judgement (the writer), and keep a deterministic prose renderer as the fallback — not "strip every string literal".

Two smaller corrections to the finding's numbers: (a) "19 facts admit 171 pairs" overstates — several of the 19 reads.push sites are mutually exclusive branches of one check, so ~13 independent facts and ~78 pairs; (b) the shipped memory caps at three days back (`for (let k = 1; k <= 3; k++)`, evidence.js:427), so "this is the third flat day running" is exactly at the edge of what it can see and a fourth would not be visible.

refuted.title: The "nobody reached the last step" warning is flush against the funnel above it
refuted.why:
REFUTED as stated. The CSS fact is right; the consequence and the fix are not.

1) DOES THE CODE EXIST? The rule text is verbatim correct, the line number is stale. `.hqp-warn { color: var(--hot2); font-size: 0.74rem; }` now sits at C:/Web Development/trymstene.com/src/pages/inbox.astro:260, not :210 — the file was edited by a concurrent process during this audit (a spacing scale `--sp1: 0.35rem; --sp2: 0.6rem; --sp3: 0.95rem; --sp4: 1.5rem; --sp5: 2.4rem;` landed at :52, `.hqp-cap` moved 76 -> 89 and switched to `margin: var(--sp1) 0 0 0.2rem`, `.hqp-trow:nth-child(even)` banding was added, `.hqp-area` moved 215 -> 288). The trailing `/* no margin */` in the quoted evidence is the claimant's annotation, not file text. The rule really does carry no margin, and grep over src/, worker-pulse/src/ and public/ finds it defined exactly once.

2) IS THE CONSEQUENCE REAL? Only in a narrow, conditional branch — and the headline is wrong.
- The mechanism claim checks out: at src/scripts/pulse-rooms.js:455 the warning is appended to `card`, which is `.hqp-area` (created :434). `.hqp-area` (inbox.astro:288) is `background: var(--hcard); border-radius: 18px; padding: 0.9rem; margin: 0 0 0.6rem; box-shadow: ...` — a plain block. No `display:grid`, no `gap`, no `> * + *` rule anywhere in the file. So nothing supplies spacing.
- But "0px of air" is FALSE for the dominant path. The preceding sibling is `.hqp-funnel` (pulse-rooms.js:439), and inbox.astro:103 gives it `padding: 0.9rem`. That puts 14.4px of the funnel's own bottom padding between the last `.hqp-flab` line and the warning — MORE air than the desk's own norms (`.hqp-cap` gets `var(--sp1)` = 5.6px at :89; `.hqp-tbl` gets `var(--sp2)` = 9.6px at :206).
- "Reads as a stray chart label" is unsupported. `.hqp-funnel` (inbox.astro:103-104) has `border-radius: 18px` and `box-shadow: 0 6px 18px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.28)`, so its bottom edge is drawn as a soft shadow band. The warning sits visibly outside that card.
- The genuinely flush branch is the `.hqp-cap` one (pulse-rooms.js:452, `margin: var(--sp1) 0 0 0.2rem` = 0 bottom). That fires for exactly ONE shop: the Banana Stand is the only `SHOPS` entry with an `aside` (src/data/pulse-dicts.js:147), and only when `stand_buy_try` is non-zero. The other three multi-step shops (Inka's cart :149, Beach Hut :151, seed shop :153) have no aside, and the LED screen :155 has one step so the `sh.steps.length > 1` guard at :454 never lets it warn at all.
- Minor factual error: the warning does not "name which storefront to fix". Its string at :455 is `'⚠ ' + nfmt(top) + ' came in and nobody reached the last step — that is the shop to work on'`. The name lives in `.hqp-aname` at the top of the card (pulse-rooms.js:435-436).

3) WOULD THE FIX WORK? No — it introduces a visible regression. The claim says "The other use (pulse-rooms.js:411...)", singular. There are TWO other uses, and it missed src/scripts/pulse-rooms.js:277: `const w = div('hqp-warn', ' ⚠ no offer', k);`. There `k` is `.hqp-tk` (created :273), a cell in the Downloads room's "Every surface that hands a file over" table. `div()` (src/scripts/hq-pulse.js:31) returns a plain block `<div>`. `.hqp-tk` (inbox.astro:219) sets `overflow: hidden`, which establishes a block formatting context so the proposed `margin-top: 0.7rem` cannot collapse away, and `.hqp-trow` (inbox.astro:208) is `display: flex; ... align-items: baseline`, so the 11.2px becomes real added height on every banded row carrying "no offer" — and pushes the tag away from the surface name it annotates (that name is `k`'s own text node, set at :274). A global `.hqp-warn` margin therefore breaks the Downloads table.
- The claim's reasoning about :411 is correct: `.hqp-aq` (inbox.astro:266) is `margin: 0.25rem 0 0.5rem`, both siblings are in-flow blocks inside the plain-block `.hqp-area`, so adjacent-sibling margins collapse to max(0.5rem, 0.7rem) = 0.7rem. That half is sound.
- Secondary problem: a hardcoded `0.7rem` matches no step of the spacing scale that just landed at inbox.astro:52.

4) ALREADY FIXED ELSEWHERE? No. One definition only (inbox.astro:260). No media query touches `.hqp-warn` — the only Pulse-region media queries are `min-width: 760px` on `.ps-rooms`, `prefers-reduced-motion` on `.ps-tickin`, and a `min-width: 620px` block for `.hqp-tiles`. No parent supplies spacing.

Net: a real but minor CSS gap (the class relies entirely on its predecessor for spacing), dressed up as a severe legibility bug it is not, with a fix that would break a third call site the claimant never found.

   · Zebra banding at :213 / :277 `nth-child(even) { background: #201a37; }` and hover at :214 / :278, under the comment at :210-212 quoting Trym's exact complaint.
   · The whole surfaces table is no longer one concatenated cell: pulse-rooms.js:270-286 now calls `grid(s5, [{h:'surface'...},{h:'took'...},{h:'saw the card'...},{h:'supported'...},{h:'no thanks'...},{h:'willing'...}], ...)`, the helper at src/scripts/hq-pulse.js:75-95, whose header comment at :62-69 names this exact table ("the downloads surfaces printed '180 · 170 · 9 · 140 · 5.3%' ... and Trym circled it in red").
   So the "unreadable header" and "no mid-separators" thirds of the claimed three-way intersection are closed. What survives is only: 40 rows still all render, and the single header never repeats.

4. THE PROPOSED FIX WOULD NOT WORK — all three parts.
   (1) Redundant: `:nth-child(5n + 1)` already does it, and the `forEach` the patch edits no longer exists (it is a `.map` feeding `grid()`).
   (2) The selector matches nothing and the mechanism is inert. `grep -rn "is-grid" src/ worker-pulse/` returns ZERO hits — `.hqp-tbl.is-grid` is invented. Sticky would not stick either way: `.hqp-tbl` carries `overflow: hidden` (inbox.astro:207) and `.hqp-grid` carries `overflow-x: auto` (inbox.astro:271), so each wrapper is itself the sticky element's scrollport, and neither scrolls vertically — `top: 0` resolves against a box that never moves. The "line 212 currently sets background: transparent" citation is wrong: line 212 is the tail of a comment (`hover works on EVERY row, not only the tappable ones. */`); the transparent head rule is inbox.astro:262 (and :280 for `.hqp-grow`). And the suggested `z-index: 1` loses to `.ps-bar { position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 5; ... background: rgba(10, 8, 20, 0.92); backdrop-filter: blur(6px); }` at inbox.astro:119-123, which already owns the viewport top.
   (3) `rows.slice(0, 12)` deletes the one thing the worker deliberately keeps. index.js:370-372: "⚠️ keep offer-only rows: a surface showing the card with NOTHING downloaded is a wiring bug, and dropping it would hide exactly that." Those rows have `files === 0`, and both sorts (worker :373, client :277) order by files descending — so they sit at the very bottom of the list, first into the bin. The default-12 cut silently removes the wiring diagnostic the filter was written to preserve.

Not verifiable from source: whether real GA4 data ever produces 40 rows. dlName (pulse-rooms.js:179-186) does append a path slug per deep page, so a long tail is plausible, but the "roughly 1,000px" scroll figure is an estimate, not a measured fact.

refuted.title: The key cell holds three stacked blocks while the row is `align-items: baseline`, so the number floats at the top of a 40px row
refuted.why:
REFUTED. The finding's central mechanism is built on a CSS rule that never applies to the element in question.

1. THE QUOTED CODE IS NOT THERE. The claim quotes `const k = div('hqp-tk', null, row);`. The actual line (pulse-rooms.js:278) is `const k = div('', null, null);` — empty class, no parent. The claim also invents `const w = div('hqp-warn', ' ⚠ no offer', k); w.title = '';`; the real line 281 is a bare one-line `if (...) div('hqp-warn', ' ⚠ no offer', k);` with no variable and no `.title`. The cited line number (274) is a column definition, not code.

2. THE CELL IS NOT `.hqp-tk`, SO THE ELLIPSIS PREMISE COLLAPSES. `div()` at hq-pulse.js:33 reads `if (cls) e.className = cls;` — an empty string is falsy, so `k` is created classless. Its only class is added by `grid()` at hq-pulse.js:88: `v.classList.add(c.num ? 'hqp-gv' : 'hqp-gk')`. Column 0 is `{ h: 'surface', w: 'minmax(11rem, 1fr)' }` with no `num`, so the cell is `.hqp-gk`. That rule (inbox.astro:288) is the entire declaration: `color: var(--hink); font-size: 0.82rem; min-width: 0;`. No `white-space: nowrap`, no `overflow: hidden`, no `text-overflow: ellipsis`, and nothing on the ancestors `.hqp-grow`/`.hqp-gin`/`.hqp-grid` sets them either. So there is no "nowrap, overflow-hidden, single-line-ellipsis box", no ellipsis being broken, and no pathology in appending block children — `.hqp-gk` is a plain block and block children are ordinary, correct markup there. `.hqp-tk` (inbox.astro:224) is a different class used by the flex `.hqp-trow` tables at pulse-rooms.js:126, 147, 155, 251, 262 — never by this grid.

3. THE ROW AND ITS LINE NUMBER ARE ALSO WRONG. The claim says `.hqp-trow` at "line 169" is `align-items: baseline` and reasons about "a flex item's baseline". This row is `.hqp-grow` (hq-pulse.js:85), at inbox.astro:280-281, and it is `display: grid`, not flex. (`.hqp-trow` is at line 213; line 169 is `.ps-hotline`.)

4. WHAT SURVIVES IS SMALL AND NOT A DEFECT. `.hqp-grow` genuinely is `align-items: baseline` (inbox.astro:281), so the numbers align to the first line box of the key cell and a warned row is taller than an unwarned one. But that is baseline alignment doing its job, and aligning the number to the *surface name* line is a defensible table convention — `center` would drag the number down to sit beside the `⚠ no offer` text or the bar instead. Note also that `.hqp-mini` is appended UNCONDITIONALLY (line 282), so every row already carries two blocks in the key cell; the stack is not warn-only as the finding implies.

5. THE ONE REAL RESIDUE IS THE BAR'S REDUNDANCY. Line 283 sizes the bar as `r.files / fmax * 70`, and `fmax` (line 269) is `Math.max(1, ...rows.map((r) => +r.files || 0))`. The very next line (284) prints `nfmt(r.files)` into the column headed `'took'` (line 272). So the bar is an unlabelled, axis-less re-encoding of the identical number two columns to its right. That observation holds on its own — but it is a footnote in the finding, not the claim under test.

6. NOT FIXED ELSEWHERE. `public/_bench-psmodes.html:166/202/203` carries a stale copy of `.hqp-tk`/`.hqp-mini`/`.hqp-warn` but does not bear on this grid.

FIX IS UNSOUND — it targets selectors that do not exist. `grep` for `is-grid` and `hqp-tname` across the whole repo returns 0 occurrences in 0 files. Every rule the fix proposes is written against `.hqp-tbl.is-grid`, which is dead CSS with literally zero effect. Beyond that: (a) the `.hqp-tname` wrap protects an ellipsis that does not exist on `.hqp-gk`; (b) `.hqp-tbl.is-grid .hqp-mini { grid-column: 1 / -1; }` is inert regardless of the selector, because `.hqp-mini` is a child of `k` (a `.hqp-gk` block), not a direct child of the grid container `.hqp-grow` — `grid-column` only applies to grid items, so the bar would have to be reparented in JS first; (c) if `align-items: center` were applied to the real selector `.hqp-grow`, it would hit every grid table on the desk, including the sources table (pulse-rooms.js:96) and campaigns (:109), which was not considered.

refuted.title: At 393px the five numbers win the width fight and the surface name ellipses away
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the claim quotes deleted code, describes a row shape that no longer exists, and proposes a fix aimed at the wrong element type.

NOTE ON LINE NUMBERS: src/pages/inbox.astro is being edited concurrently during this audit (it grew 2501 → 2505 lines between my first and last read, `git diff --stat` shows 137 changed lines uncommitted). All numbers below are from the final read.

1. THE LINE IS WRONG AND THE QUOTE IS STALE.
Line 173 of src/pages/inbox.astro is not CSS at all — it is inside the `.ps-ticker` comment block ("Padding alone does NOT fix a marquee: the text scrolls THROUGH the padding box to x=0").
`.hqp-tk` is at line 224 and does match: `.hqp-tk { font-size: 0.82rem; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }`
`.hqp-tv` is at lines 227-228 and does NOT match. The claim quotes `color: var(--hdim); font-size: 0.76rem`. The file says `color: var(--hink); font-size: var(--num-md); font-weight: 700;`. Worse, the two comment lines directly above it (225-226) exist specifically to record that the quoted version was killed: "⚠️ THIS WAS INVERTED. The value was --hdim at 0.76rem under a key in full ink at 0.82rem, so every table on the desk whispered its own numbers." The claim is quoting the pre-fix source. `--num-md` is 0.88rem (line 59), so even the width arithmetic uses the wrong font metrics — the numbers are now BIGGER and bolder than the claim assumes.

2. THE FIVE-VALUE ROW DOES NOT EXIST IN `.hqp-tv`, AND WAS ALREADY FIXED.
Every single `.hqp-tv` in the codebase — there are six — carries one value, or at most two:
  pulse-rooms.js:127 `nfmt(e.v) + (e.u ? '  ·  ' + nfmt(e.u) + ' people' : '')`
  pulse-rooms.js:148 `nfmt(p.v)` · :156 `nfmt(c.v)` · :252 `nfmt(v)` · :263 `''` · :424 `nfmt(e.v)`
The claim's own example — a surface name plus five values ending in a percentage — is the downloads table, and it was migrated out of `.hqp-trow` some time ago. inbox.astro:270-273 documents it: "The downloads panel used to print '180 · 170 · 9 · 140 · 5.3%' into ONE cell beneath a five-word header, and Trym circled it in red as unreadable." The same fix is documented again at hq-pulse.js:62-74. That table is now `grid(s5, [...6 cols...])` at pulse-rooms.js:270-286, rendering `.hqp-gk`/`.hqp-gv` inside `.hqp-gin` / `.hqp-grid`.

3. IN THAT REAL TABLE THE DESCRIBED FAILURE IS STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE.
`.hqp-grid { overflow-x: auto }` (274) wraps `.hqp-gin { display: grid; ... min-width: max-content }` (278). Because the inner grid is sized to max-content, the `minmax(11rem, 1fr)` surface column resolves to its full intrinsic width and the TABLE scrolls sideways inside itself instead of the page. And `.hqp-gk` (287) is `color: var(--hink); font-size: 0.82rem; min-width: 0;` — it has no `overflow: hidden` and no `text-overflow: ellipsis`, so it cannot render "The gallery…" under any width. "The gallery" is a DL_NAME (src/data/pulse-dicts.js:65, `['/banana-memes/','The gallery']`), which confirms the claim's example row belongs to this grid, not to `.hqp-trow`.

4. THE CITED HOUSE-STYLE PRECEDENT IS AT THE WRONG LINES.
The claim cites inbox.astro:407-410 for `.hq-row__who { grid-column: 1 / -1; }`. Lines 405-410 are `.bm-empty` / `.bm-fine` / an unrelated `@media (max-width: 480px)`. The real rules are `.hq-row__who { min-width: 0; }` at 472 and `.hq-row__who { grid-column: 1 / -1; }` at 486, inside the `@media (max-width: 560px)` block that opens at 484.

5. NOT FIXED "ELSEWHERE" IN THE SENSE THE CLAIM MEANS — because there is nothing to fix. There is no `@media (max-width: 560px)` block touching any `.hqp-` or `.ps-` class anywhere in the file; the nine media queries are at 144, 197, 320, 348, 414, 484, 534, 556, 628 and all target `.ps-rooms`, `.hqp-tiles`, or `.bm-*`/`.hq-row` on the users and dev desks.

RESIDUAL, reported for honesty and NOT a finding: `.hqp-tk` can still ellipse in renderNow's live-pages table (pulse-rooms.js:147 puts a full page TITLE in the key while :148 puts one short number in the value). But the value there is at most ~5 characters, so the name keeps roughly 290px of the ~327px row — nowhere near the ~93px / twelve-character collapse the claim describes. The claimed consequence is not real at the claimed magnitude anywhere on the desk.

refuted.title: In every table row the value is dimmer AND smaller than its own label
refuted.why:
REFUTED against the current source; the defect was real at HEAD but is already fixed in the working tree.

(1) WRONG LINE. src/pages/inbox.astro:173-174 currently contains `.ps-hotline { background: rgba(94, 224, 138, 0.12); color: var(--ok); border-radius: var(--r-sm); padding: 0.5rem 0.8rem; font-size: 0.78rem; margin: 0 0 var(--sp2); }` — not the table rules. (3) ALREADY FIXED IN THE WORKING TREE.
