refuted.title: The funnel repeats the inversion, and buries its most useful number at 11px
The analyst exists twice as two class families that have drifted 0.01rem apart
refuted.why:
REFUTED as stated. The CSS values in the evidence table are real, but every line number is wrong, and the load-bearing assertion — "Both render the same payload" — is false. The `.hqp-a*` copy is unreachable dead code, so no reader ever meets the analyst typeset two ways.

1. DOES THE FILE/LINE CONTAIN THAT CODE? No.
- inbox.astro:227 (the FILE line the finding is filed against) is `       hover works on EVERY row, not only the tappable ones. */` — the tail of a comment about table row banding. It is not analyst CSS.
- The claimed range 227-241 is the TABLE family: `.hqp-trow:hover` (229), `.hqp-trow:nth-child(5n+1)` (232), `.hqp-tk` (234-235), `.hqp-tv` (238-239), `.hqp-tv.is-zero` (240).
- The real `.hqp-a*` analyst family is inbox.astro:315-328. Every cited number is ~88 lines low: `.hqp-ahead` is 323 not 235, `.hqp-abody` 324 not 236, `.hqp-aread` 325 not 237, `.hqp-aicon` 326 not 238, `.hqp-atext` 327 not 239, `.hqp-arec` 328 not 240, `.hqp-verdict` 317 not 229.
- The real `.ps-*` family is inbox.astro:255-265, ~66 lines off: `.ps-verdict` 255 not 189, `.ps-rhead` 260 not 194, `.ps-rbody` 261 not 195, `.ps-read` 262 not 196, `.ps-ricon` 263 not 197, `.ps-rtext` 264 not 198, `.ps-rec` 265 not 199.
- "Inline copy (hq-pulse.js:193-203)" is wrong too: 193-203 is `export function funnel(host, steps)`. The analyst render is hq-pulse.js:229-239. Only "pulse-shell.js:283-294" is roughly right (the render runs 286-294).
- The VALUES are all accurate. I confirmed each one verbatim at its true line.

2. IS THE CONSEQUENCE REAL? No. The `.hqp-a*` markup is emitted only by `googleBlock()`, hq-pulse.js:212. That function is (a) not exported — hq-pulse.js:31-242 exports div, nfmt, pct, section, grid, tile, lineChart, barsH, rate, funnel, renderLedger, and nothing else — and (b) `grep -c googleBlock src/scripts/hq-pulse.js` returns **1**, the definition itself. A repo-wide grep over every .js/.astro/.mjs finds the same single hit. It has no caller anywhere.
Git says exactly when it died: `git show ed18f4d9 -- src/scripts/hq-pulse.js` contains `-  googleBlock(el, data.analyst, data.live);`. Commit ed18f4d9 "Pulse 2.0: the analyst overlay and the room badges" — the same commit that introduced `.ps-rhead` — removed the only call site and left the function and its stylesheet block standing. `renderLedger` (hq-pulse.js:242-410) never references `analyst` or `live` again.
So there is exactly ONE live analyst surface, the overlay at pulse-shell.js:286-294. The reader cannot meet the analyst in the ledger room. "The same nine lines typeset two different ways depending on which room the reader met them in" describes something that has not happened since ed18f4d9.

Corroborating proof the `.hqp-*` copy is a corpse rather than a live sibling: the verdict vocabularies do not even overlap. analyst.js emits verdict ∈ {notable (112,128,135,142,155), quiet (163,179), thin (173), no-baseline (243)}. `.ps-verdict` styles precisely those four (inbox.astro:257 is-notable, 258 is-quiet, 259 is-thin/is-no-baseline). `.hqp-verdict` styles is-good/is-up/is-watch/is-down/is-bad/is-alarm (320-322) — not one of which the analyst has ever emitted. And hq-pulse.js:230 falls back to `'normal'` and prints the raw token, while pulse-shell.js:286 falls back to `'quiet'` and maps through `VLABEL`. That is not 0.01rem of drift; that is an older schema.
(No override rescues it either: the `<style>` at inbox.astro:12 is `is:inline`, so unscoped — the classes would match if they were ever rendered. The media queries at 331-335 touch only `.hqp-tiles`.)

3. WOULD THE FIX WORK? No, three ways.
- Applied literally it deletes inbox.astro:227-241, which is the table family. `.hqp-tk`/`.hqp-tv`/`.hqp-trow` back every table on the desk (`.hqp-tv` alone is the number column). It would strip the ink, the tabular-nums, the ellipsis and the banding off every row in the ledger, downloads, shop and world rooms. And "have hq-pulse.js:193-203 emit the .ps-* classes" would rewrite `funnel()`.
- Applied to the CORRECT lines it is still a no-op on screen: renaming classes inside a function with no callers changes nothing a reader sees, while leaving the actual defect (29 lines of unreachable JS) in place.
- The "pure class rename, no markup change" premise is false anyway. `.ps-rcard` is the modal panel — `position: relative; width: min(640px, 100%); border-radius: 22px; padding: 1.4rem 1.1rem 1.2rem; box-shadow: 0 20px 50px` (inbox.astro:249-251) — not an in-page card like `.hqp-analyst` (315-316). The fix deletes `.hqp-analyst` without naming a replacement container, so googleBlock's card would render unstyled or, if given `.ps-rcard`, would drop a 640px-capped modal panel inline inside a section.
- "removes seven declarations" undercounts: the block is 8 rules over 14 lines.

4. ALREADY FIXED? Yes, at the level that mattered. ed18f4d9 de-duplicated the analyst by deleting the call, not the code. What remains is a corpse, not a live second copy — so design-library.md:120 §5 "One layer, not per-surface copies" / :130 "Two copies drift within a week" is not the rule being broken. There is one layer. There is also litter.

There IS a real, smaller finding underneath, which the claim mis-diagnosed: dead code left by ed18f4d9 — `googleBlock()` at hq-pulse.js:212-240 (29 lines, no caller, not exported) and its stylesheet block at inbox.astro:315-328 (14 lines). Worth deleting, but as "remove the corpse", not "reconcile two drifting families".

refuted.title: The event-lens select is 460px wide and 82px of it is cut off the screen
refuted.why:
REFUTED — already fixed, and the quoted evidence is a stale copy of the file.

1. THE CITED LINE IS WRONG. inbox.astro:141 is `.ps-rooms { display: flex; gap: 0.4rem; overflow-x: auto; ... }` — the room strip, not the lens. `.ps-lens` is at 169-171 and `.ps-modes` at 166-167. The claim's second cited line, "`.bm-wrap select { font-size: 16px }` at inbox.astro:250", is also wrong: line 250 is inside `.ps-rcard`; the 16px rule is at 337-338.

2. THE QUOTED CSS IS THE PRE-FIX VERSION. The claim's text (`padding: 0.3rem 0.6rem`, no max-width; `.ps-modes { gap: 0.4rem; ... margin: 0.6rem 0 0.4rem }`) matches commit c67cbc53 ("Pulse 2.0: the living half") exactly. Commit 1c418c3f ("Give the desk one spacing scale and one way to print a number") superseded it, adding `max-width: 100%` to `.ps-lens` and splitting the three chips into a `.ps-mchips` wrapper (inbox.astro:168, built at pulse-shell.js:143). The claim was audited against the old file.

3. MEASURED ON THE CURRENT CSS, THE OVERFLOW DOES NOT EXIST. I built a bench from the verbatim inbox.astro <style> block + public/css/styles.css + fonts.css, with the DOM pulse-shell.js:140-158 actually creates and the real EV_LABEL option strings, and drove it with the repo's own Playwright:
   - 393px: select x 14.4, width 364.2, right edge 378.6 — 14px INSIDE the viewport. `.ps-modes` scrollWidth 364 == clientWidth 364. `.ps-body` 364/364. documentElement.scrollWidth 393 == clientWidth 393. No overflow anywhere.
   - 360px: width 331.2, right 345.6. Also clean.
   - 1280px: width 433, sits inline beside the chips as designed.
   The screenshot shows a complete pill with its right edge and the native dropdown arrow. Not a broken input.

4. WHY max-width ALONE IS ENOUGH (the claim says `min-width: 0` is "the load-bearing half" — it is not). Per CSS Flexbox §4.5, a flex item's automatic minimum size is the content size suggestion "further clamped by the maximum main size property if that is definite". `max-width: 100%` against a definite-width flex container is definite, so it clamps `min-width: auto` too. Measurement confirms it: computed `min-width` is still `auto` and computed `flex` is still `0 1 auto`, yet the select shrank from its 433px intrinsic width to exactly the 364px container width.

5. THE MECHANISM WAS REAL — I reproduced it. Forcing `.ps-lens { max-width: none !important }` gives width 433, right edge 447.4, `.ps-modes` scrollWidth 433 vs clientWidth 364, `overflow-x: visible`, and `html { overflow-x: clip }` (public/css/styles.css:55, body at :73) swallowing it with no scrollbar. So the diagnosis was correct for the old code; it is 433px not the claimed 460.2px because of the padding change in 1c418c3f. The supporting sub-claims also still hold: the select does compute to 16px (`.bm-wrap select` at 0-1-1 beats `.ps-lens` at 0-1-0), the widest option is EV_LABEL['offer_world'] = 'chose Banana World from the card 🌍 (retired 27 Aug)' (pulse-events.js:34, in LENSES at pulse-shell.js:24-26), and 'live' is the default room (pulse-shell.js:66). But those were the ingredients of a bug that is now fixed — the 16px is deliberate (inbox.astro:337, "form controls never below 16px → iOS won't zoom-jump on focus").

No media query touches `.ps-lens` or `.ps-modes` (the only @media rules in the file are at 144, 197, 331, 359, 425, 495, 545, 567, 639), so nothing else is masking or contributing.

Math.round(((cur - base) / base) * 100) : null);` — whose fallback branch is `: null`, not the claimed `: (cur ? null : 0)`. That exact string is in no file in the repo.

(2) The mechanism described is the RETIRED algorithm. The claim's decision variable is mean(recent3) vs mean(early4). The live test is levelShift() at evidence.js:108-124, which uses median() (lines 111-113) and a triple gate at line 121: `if (sep < 2.2 || p == null || Math.abs(p) < 40 || absGap < 25) return null;`. evidence.js:100 names the claim's algorithm as the replaced one: "The old test compared mean(last 3 days) with mean(first 4) and fired at 35%." The exported `mean` (evidence.js:20) is imported by nothing.

(3) The claimed symptom does not exist. `grep -rn "🚀"` over worker-pulse/src/ and src/scripts/ returns nothing. The level headline is analyst.js:144, plain text "The site has settled at a new level, about N sessions a day." The level fact is explicitly excluded from the emoji `reads` list at analyst.js:192 (`x.id !== 'level'`), so iconFor() never runs on it. shapeOf() at analyst.js:45 only gives it the headline when daysRunning <= 1; on the second morning it degrades to 'settled' (line 52).

(4) The measured magnitudes are wrong by 30-60x in the claim's own scenario. Running the real exported levelShift over 200k lognormal trials at a flat 45/day site: cv=0.15 fires up 0.005% / down 0.002% (claim: 3.25% / 0.56%); cv=0.20 up 0.10% / down 0.04% (claim: 5.85% / 1.60%); cv=0.30 up 1.12% / down 0.55% (claim: 12.31% / 5.45%). At Trym's ~45/day organic level this fires about once a quarter, not daily.

(5) A real asymmetry does exist underneath, but it is a different defect and worse than claimed. A deterministic ratio probe (before flat, after flat) shows which gate binds. At before=45 the binding gate is `absGap < 25`, NOT pct: down fires only at ratio <= 0.44 (after=20), up at >= 1.56 (after=70), while |p|>=40 is already met at 0.60/1.40 — so the claim blames the wrong variable in the exact regime it simulated. At before=120 and before=300 the binding gate IS `Math.abs(p) < 40`, firing at r=1.40 up and r=0.60 down (ln 1.4 = 0.336 vs |ln 0.6| = 0.511), and measured flat-site up:down is 10.7:1 at cv=0.20 and 53-69:1 at cv=0.15 — far beyond the claimed 2-6:1. refuted.title: The 6-point engagement gate fires on 49% of days at 45 sessions — it is below one standard error
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the analysis is statistically correct but the code it describes no longer exists in the codebase under audit, and the defect is already fixed by a better mechanism.

1. FILE/LINE CHECK — FAILS.
C:\Web Development\trymstene.com\worker-pulse\src\analyst.js line 192 actually reads:
    fresh.filter((x) => x.id !== 'level' && x.id !== 'money' && x.id !== 'blackout')
      .slice(0, 3).forEach((x) => reads.push({ icon: iconFor(x), text: x.say }));
There is no `pE`, no `avgE`, and no 6-point gate anywhere in that file. It is 262 lines, not the 433 the brief states, and index.js calls analyse() at line 671, not ~639.
`grep -rn "Math.abs(pE)"` finds the quoted code at exactly one path: .claude/worktrees/silly-tharp-f872a3/worker-pulse/src/analyst.js:191-192 — a stale Claude Code agent worktree checked out at detached d4126b2a ("The greeter keeps to her pen..."), which `git merge-base --is-ancestor d4126b2a main` confirms is an ANCESTOR of main. The claim was written against an old checkout. (Corroborating: the claim cites "the file's own header (lines 11-14)" for the horoscope rule — that is the old file's header exactly; in the current file lines 11-14 are the "He was right, for two separate reasons" preamble and the horoscope rule has moved to lines 23-25.)

2. WAS THE CONSEQUENCE REAL IN THAT OLD FILE? YES, and precisely so.
I re-implemented the old gate exactly (mean of the 7 baseline rates, Math.round to whole points so the true threshold is 5.5, `thin = S < MIN_RATE_N` with MIN_RATE_N = 40) and ran 200,000 simulated days per cell with engagement held perfectly constant:
    n=45, p=0.50 -> 48.6% fire   (claim: 48.8%)
    n=45, p=0.35 -> 46.6%        (claim: 46.6%)
    n=100, p=0.50 -> 30.2%       (claim: 30.5%)
    n=300, p=0.50 ->  7.5%       (claim:  7.4%)
The sd of (E - mean-of-7) at n=45, p=0.5 is 100*sqrt(0.25/45*(1+1/7)) = 7.97 points, as claimed. Nothing in the old file mitigated it: the engagement read is `read(2, ...)` (worktree analyst.js:203), and the verdict block at worktree analyst.js:370-394 is `reads.sort(...); const loud = reads.filter((r) => r.weight >= 2);` then `else { verdict = 'notable'; ... headline = first.slice(0, cut)... }` where `first = loud[0].text`. So a single weight-2 read both forces 'notable' AND can own the headline. The old file had no memory of what it had said before, so it repeated daily. The claim's diagnosis of the old file is sound.

3. ALREADY FIXED — this is decisive.
`git log -S "Math.abs(pE) >= 6" -- worker-pulse/src/analyst.js` shows the gate was introduced in 9faf73f8 and REMOVED in 25ecb4d9 ("Say why Google is not answering"), which is on main and an ancestor of HEAD (db042986). The engagement fact was moved to worker-pulse/src/evidence.js:204-218:
    const ptsE = Math.round((E - median(baseE)) * 100);                       // :207
    const zE = robustZ(E * 100, baseE.map((x) => x * 100));                   // :208
    sig: S < MIN_RATE_N ? 0 : sigOf(zE, S, Math.abs(ptsE)),                   // :213
with robustZ at evidence.js:40-45 — `const s = Math.max(mad(base), Math.max(1.5, m * 0.12)); return (cur - m) / s;` — and sigOf at evidence.js:72-77 requiring `a >= Z_LOUD` (Z_LOUD = 2.4, evidence.js:68) for sig 2.
The fixed constant is gone. The gate is now scaled by the week's own observed MAD, which is implicitly n-aware: at 45 sessions the observed day-to-day scatter of engagement is itself ~7.5 points, so sig 2 demands roughly a 18-point move — almost exactly the ~16 points the claim says is the honest answer at that volume. Running the same 200k-day simulation against the SHIPPED gate:
    n=45, p=0.50 -> 4.4% loud (sig>=2)   [was 48.6%]
    n=45, p=0.35 -> 8.7%                 [was 46.6%]
    n=100, p=0.50 -> 0.8%                [was 30.2%]
    n=300, p=0.50 -> 0.0%                [was  7.5%]
Two further dampers exist that the old file lacked: analyst.js:109 `const fresh = loud.filter((x) => x.daysRunning <= 1);` and shapeOf() at analyst.js:46 `const fresh = pack.facts.filter((x) => x.sig >= 2 && x.daysRunning <= 1); if (fresh.length) return 'break';` — so a loud engagement fact on its second morning no longer forces verdict='notable' at all; it falls through to 'settled'/'quiet'.

4. WOULD THE PROPOSED FIX WORK? NO — it would be a regression, and it has three defects of its own.
   (a) `sumBaseSessions` is not defined anywhere in the repo (`grep -rn "sumBaseSessions" --include=*.js` returns nothing). The patch would not run.
   (b) It reverts to mean + a normal SE, directly against the doctrine written into evidence.js:29-31: "MEDIAN + MAD, NOT MEAN + SD. One ad day in a seven-day window drags the mean up and inflates the sd, so the days after it read as 'normal' and the ad day itself reads as unremarkable — exactly backwards." On this specific site (ad flights, level changes) that is the failure mode that matters.
   (c) The SE model is wrong for the data. It treats engagement as pure binomial noise around a stable p. Real days carry genuine variation on top (weekday/weekend, source mix, an ad flight), so a pure-binomial SE UNDERSTATES the true spread and the gate would still over-fire. robustZ measures the actual observed spread and absorbs both sources at once.
   (d) `p(1-p)/sumBaseSessions` is only the correct variance for avgE if all seven baseline days have equal sessions. `avgE` is an unweighted mean of seven rates, so the correct term is (1/49)*Sum_i p(1-p)/n_i. On a week containing one 300-session ad day and six 40-session days the pooled form understates it materially.
   (e) The claim's own reference figure is wrong by its own model: requiring 1.96*sd = 6 points WITH the (1+1/7) baseline term it introduces two sentences earlier gives n = 0.25*(8/7)/(6/196)^2 = 305, not 267. 267 is what you get only by dropping that term.

VERDICT: the statistical work is excellent and would have been a genuine finding against d4126b2a. Against the codebase as it stands it names a line that holds different code, in a file that no longer contains the mechanism, describing a bug that commit 25ecb4d9 already fixed — and its proposed replacement is weaker than what shipped and would not execute.

The mean/sd estimator was deliberately swapped for median/MAD — evidence.js lines 29-31: "⚠️ MEDIAN + MAD, NOT MEAN + SD. One ad day in a seven-day window drags the mean up and inflates the sd..." `mad()` is at lines 32-36 with the 1.4826 consistency constant.

At median 300 a real week's MAD-based sd is well above 36, so the floor does not bind at all on ordinary high-traffic weeks; it binds only on the freakishly steady week the comment at lines 38-39 names as its purpose.

refuted.title: The campaign "tension worth watching" is forced by GA4's own definitions, not by a signal
refuted.why:
REFUTED — on three independent grounds: the named file/line does not hold the code, the defect is already deleted from shipping code, and the load-bearing conclusion is unsupported.

The brief's landmarks confirm the audit was commissioned against that snapshot ("433 lines"; "analyse() at ~639" → worktree 636, main 671; "<style> ~44-249" → worktree block closes at 331, main at 641). So the reviewer read real code, but code main has moved past.

2) ALREADY FIXED. Commit 25ecb4d9 "Say why Google is not answering" (ancestor of main HEAD b37afad3; working tree clean) rewrote analyst.js 626→261 lines and extracted evidence.js. It deleted the `cSecs < 20 && cEng >= 40` block entirely — read, rec and all. The successor is one campaign fact at worker-pulse/src/evidence.js:255-274: it still computes `const cEng` (line 262) and `const cSecs` (line 263), but they appear only inside `say`; significance is `sig: c.sessions < MIN_STEP_N ? 0 : (Math.abs(gap) >= 10 ? 2 : 1)` (line 266) — engagement gap against the site only. No dwell threshold anywhere, no recommendation. `grep -n "secs\b"` across analyst.js / evidence.js / writer.js on main returns exactly two hits, both in evidence.js, neither a threshold.

3) THE MECHANISM VERIFIES, THE CONCLUSION DOES NOT. Verified correct in the snapshot: `const cEng = Math.round(rate(paid.engaged, paid.sessions) * 100)` (line 219) and `const cSecs = Math.round(rate(paid.secs, paid.sessions))` (line 220); index.js:625-627 maps `sessions: met(r,0), engaged: met(r,1), secs: met(r,2)` off metrics `sessions / engagedSessions / userEngagementDuration` (index.js:583-584), so the denominators are exactly as claimed. Weight 2 → notable is real: `const loud = reads.filter((r) => r.weight >= 2)` (line 371), `else { verdict = 'notable' }` (line 394) — and STRONGER than claimed, since line 396 slices `loud[0].text` into the HEADLINE, so on a day with no earlier weight-2 read this read leads the report. Rec slots verify: `const rec = (text, because) => { if (recs.length < 3) recs.push(...) }` (line 133), and line 244 is that rec call.

But "an arithmetic identity dressed as an insight" is not what was demonstrated. Two ratios sharing a denominator are not one statistic: cEng counts sessions crossing GA4's engagement bar (10s OR 2+ pageviews OR a conversion), cSecs averages focus-seconds over ALL sessions. The conjunction selects a real region — wide but shallow — and the reviewer's own derivation converts it into a substantive threshold ("engaged visitors averaged under ~46 seconds"), which is the opposite of a tautology. The finding then rests entirely on the unsupported empirical assertion that this is "true of essentially all paid traffic". Nothing in the file supports it, and the site's own recorded paid-dwell figures (35s at the least sticky area, 140s at the rave) point the other way: a campaign averaging even 35s/session gives cSecs ≈ 35 and never trips cSecs < 20. The rule is more plausibly near-silent than always-on, so the claimed consequence — that it burns a rec slot and forces 'notable' as a matter of course — is not established.

WHAT THE REVIEWER ACTUALLY FOUND AND MISSED: the implied bar SLIDES with cEng. With mean unengaged dwell u ≈ 3s, cSecs < 20 means engaged dwell below ≈45.5s at cEng 40%, ≈31s at 60%, ≈24s at 80%, 20s at 100%. So the BETTER a campaign's engagement, the shallower it must be to trip an alarm whose sentence reads "engagement is fine but dwell is only Xs" — backwards. And the Xs it prints is diluted by the bouncers, so the figure quoted is not the dwell of the people the sentence claims to describe. That is a genuine defect, but it is a different one, in the opposite direction, and it is moot: the code is gone.

refuted.title: The analyst has no memory of what it said yesterday, and worker-pulse has nowhere to keep one

The finding is still REFUTED, because its headline claim — "the analyst has no memory of what it said yesterday" — is false on the working tree it was written against. evidence.js:415-435 solves exactly this by deterministic re-derivation instead of storage: buildPack re-runs buildFacts with upTo = days.length - k for k = 1..3, collects the sig>=2 fact ids each of those mornings would have produced, and stamps daysRunning on every fact. The pack then ships an explicit instruction (evidence.js:457-459) that a fact with daysRunning >= 2 "was already reported on previous mornings and must not lead again", and writer.js:89-92 makes that rule 4 of the system prompt, calling it "the single most important thing". analyst.js:19-21 names this as the second of the two fixes in this very change. Re-derivation is in one respect strictly better than the proposed stored log: it has no holes on mornings nobody opened the page.

The claim also misidentifies the file. It cites "analyst.js line 77 (pure function over one 8-day window)" and the brief's "433 lines". analyst.js is 261 lines; line 77 is a bare `}` closing the second cross-fact block in crossFacts(); analyse() is at line 239. The claim was written against a pre-change analyst.js and does not describe the code that is there now.

What genuinely survives, and it is much narrower than "the analyst has amnesia":
1. The claim's own example — "the fifth flat day in a row" — is real but is NOT a storage problem. evidence.js:434 reads `f.daysRunning = f.sig >= 2 ? n : 0`, so on a flat morning where nothing clears sig 2, every fact's daysRunning is 0 and there is no streak counter at all. Quiet is the one state the streak machinery does not track.
2. The look-back is capped at k <= 3 (evidence.js:427), so daysRunning maxes at 4. With the 8-day pull it could already reach 5 before buildFacts bails at `base.length < 3` (evidence.js:148). Both are one-line limits, not missing infrastructure.
3. Only the writer's prose is truly unpersisted: writeReport's output is merged into `data` (index.js:687) and put in rspCache (index.js:692), and `pack` is stripped before the response (index.js:680), so nothing keeps the last headlines. That, and only that, actually needs storage.

It is never called. `renderLedger` (src/scripts/hq-pulse.js:242-332) reads only `data.roll` (243) and `data.world` (244); nothing in its 90 lines touches `data.analyst` or `data.live`. `git show ed18f4d9 -- src/scripts/hq-pulse.js` proves when the caller went: the commit "Pulse 2.0: the analyst overlay and the room badges" removed `-  googleBlock(el, data.analyst, data.live);` from what is now the stray double blank line at hq-pulse.js:248-249. So the claimed consequence — "Every day the desk card renders is-notable / is-quiet / is-thin ... the pill is always the same dim grey" — is wrong on its own terms. The "What Google saw" section (hq-pulse.js:214), the `.hqp-analyst` card (229), the headline (231), body (232), reads (233-237), recs (238) and confidence caption (239) are all unreachable, along with nine CSS rules at inbox.astro:315-328.

refuted.title: DESIGN DECISION: the evidence pack + LLM writer contract, with the grounding check that must gate it
refuted.why:
REFUTED on two independent grounds: the quoted evidence does not exist at that line, and the entire proposal is already built and committed at HEAD.

1. THE LINE IS WRONG. worker-pulse/src/index.js:639 is `for (const r of rows(evR)) {` — the GA4 event-row fill loop, not an analyse() call. I checked both the working tree and `git show HEAD:worker-pulse/src/index.js` (identical in this region), so it is not a stale-snapshot artefact. The quoted string `const out = analyse({ days, events, eventUsers, campaigns, gsc, gscBase });` exists NOWHERE in the file: the real call is at 671-672 and passes three more inputs — `sources`, `world`, `areas: WORLD_DOORS`. The quoted `const data = { ...out, date: yDate, ... }` also does not exist; line 680-681 is `const { pack, ...det } = out;` / `let data = { ...det, date: yDate, niceDate: nice, generatedAt: Date.now(), by: 'rules' };`. Every numeral and every string in the QUOTED EVIDENCE block is fabricated or months stale.

2. THE FIX IS ALREADY SHIPPED, nearly beat-for-beat. The initial git-status snapshot listed evidence.js and writer.js as untracked, but `git status --porcelain` now returns clean and `git cat-file -e HEAD:worker-pulse/src/writer.js` succeeds — both files are committed, and index.js:7-8 imports `analyse` and `writeReport`.

   - PACK: worker-pulse/src/evidence.js `buildPack()` (line 421) returns `{ sessions, baselineSessions, levelChanged, daysOfHistory, sampleIsThin, rules, counts, facts, quietFacts }`. `fact()` at evidence.js:85-97 emits `{ id, area, label, value, unit, base, deltaPct, deltaPctText, n, z, sig, daysRunning, say, because }`. The claim's `gate`/`salience` is `sig` (evidence.js:72-79, the 0/1/2/3 ladder); its `streak`/`prior[]` is `daysRunning`, computed at evidence.js:427-435 by RE-RUNNING the fact engine for the three prior days — a stronger mechanism than the proposed prior-headline list, because it is derived, not remembered.
   - PROMPT CONTRACT: worker-pulse/src/writer.js:63-104. Rule 1 = "NEVER WRITE A NUMBER THAT IS NOT IN THE EVIDENCE… You may not add, subtract, divide, round or estimate" (the claim's rule 1). Rule 2 = the horoscope rule (claim's rule 3). Rule 3 = small-n (claim's rule 3/n-carrying). Rule 4 = "DO NOT LEAD WITH SOMETHING YOU LED WITH YESTERDAY… Facts carry daysRunning" (claim's rule 4/5). Rule 5 = connect facts, "If you find none, do not manufacture one" (claim's rule 6). Rule 7 = at most two recs, evidence-backed (claim's rule 7).
   - OUTPUT: writer.js:42-61 is a strict `json_schema` on `output_config.format`, required `['verdict','headline','body','reads','recs','confidence']`, verdict enum `['notable','quiet','thin','no-baseline']` — the claim's exact shape, and constrained rather than requested.
   - GROUNDING CHECK: writer.js:106-141. `numsIn()` uses `/-?\d[\d,._]*\d|-?\d/g`, `allowedNumbers(pack)` walks the pack at any depth adding every numeric and every numeral inside every string plus a `SAFE` set, and `ungrounded()` scans headline+body+reads+recs+confidence. writer.js:185-190 DISCARDS on any hit: `return { __err: 'writer invented numbers (' + bad.slice(0,6).join(', ') + ')' }`.
   - FALLBACK: index.js:680-691 computes the deterministic report FIRST (`by: 'rules'`) and only overlays the written one on success — the claim's `source:'rules'` flag is the existing `by` field.

3. RENDERER CITATION ALSO WRONG. pulse-shell.js:283-296 is correct (the verdict/headline/body/reads/recs/confidence block). But hq-pulse.js:193-203 is `export function funnel(host, steps)` — the funnel-bar renderer, unrelated. The analyst renderer in that file is at hq-pulse.js:228-238.

4. WHAT IS GENUINELY MISSING is only the tail of the proposal, and the claim gets one detail right by accident: worker-pulse/wrangler.toml really does declare no bindings (only `[vars] PROPERTY_ID`, `GSC_SITE`). The only cache is `rspCache`, an in-memory `Map` (index.js:39) with a 30-minute TTL at index.js:585-586 (`if (hit && Date.now() - hit.t < 1800000)`). So "one model call per day / the same words on every reload" is NOT true today — a new isolate or a lunchtime reload past 30 minutes re-calls the model and Trym gets different prose for the same day. And writer.js:33 defaults to `claude-opus-5` at `max_tokens: 16000` (writer.js:160), so the claim's "one small-model call per day — negligible" understates the real cost profile by a wide margin. Second real gap: nothing on the desk reads `by` — grep for `an.by`, `.written`, `writerNote` across pulse-shell.js, hq-pulse.js, pulse-rooms.js and inbox.astro returns zero hits, and index.js:689 says so itself (`// shown nowhere; read it in the payload`). That is exactly the failure the claim names ("a silent outage changing the voice one morning without explanation") and it is the one mitigation that was specified and not wired up.

critic.title: Three text classes fail 4.5:1 because opacity is stacked on --hdim
critic.evidence: `.hqp-tsub { color: var(--hdim); font-size: 0.72rem; opacity: 0.8; … }` (:85), `.hqp-rsub { color: var(--hdim); font-size: 0.68rem; opacity: 0.75; … }` (:110), `.hqp-foot { color: var(--hdim); font-size: 0.72rem; opacity: 0.75; … }` (:330). `--hdim` #9a90b8 on `--hcard` #1c1631 is 5.85:1; composited at 0.8 it is 4.23:1 and at 0.75 it is 3.83:1. All three are normal-size text (11.5px and 10.9px), so the 4.5:1 threshold applies.
critic.why: `.hqp-tsub` is the second line of every KPI tile — it carries the delta arrow and the denominator, i.e. the context that makes the big number mean anything — and it is the least legible text on the desk. `.hqp-rsub` carries "needs 20 · has 7", the honesty gate. Recession by multiplier also makes the value unpredictable: the same class over `--hpanel` and over `--hcard` lands at two different contrasts.
critic.fix: Delete `opacity` from :85, :110 and :330 and let the new `--prose-s` size do the recession. If a third ink is genuinely wanted, add it as a token — `--hsoft: #8b81a6`, ~4.9:1 on `--hcard` — and never as a multiplier. Same treatment for `.ps-rbadge`'s `opacity: 0.8` (:150).

critic.title: Captions are still indented 3.2px off every other left edge on the desk
critic.evidence: inbox.astro:95 `.hqp-cap { color: var(--hdim); font-size: 0.76rem; line-height: 1.5; margin: var(--sp1) 0 0 0.2rem; }` — a fourth value nobody else on the desk uses. `.hqp-cap` appears under charts (pulse-rooms.js:88), under bar sets (hq-pulse.js:292, :295), and inside `.hqp-area` cards (pulse-rooms.js:415, :454).
critic.why: One of the two spacing findings that survived unfixed. Every heading, note, table and tile starts at x=0 of its container; the caption starts 3.2px in, so a column of left edges has one wobble in it — visible precisely because everything else was straightened.
critic.fix: `margin: var(--sp1) 0 0;`. Then add the missing bottom gap for the case the auditors correctly identified: `.hqp-sec > .hqp-cap { margin-bottom: var(--sp3); }` and `.hqp-sec > .hqp-cap:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }` — captions inside `.hqp-area` and `.hqp-analyst` are not `.hqp-sec` children so they stay put.

critic.title: `.hqp-sec` still has no top margin, so a section nested in a card sits flush
critic.evidence: inbox.astro:66 `.hqp-sec { margin: 0 0 var(--sp5); }` — bottom only. hq-pulse.js:310 opens a second section inside the world block (`s = section(el, 'Is anyone visiting', …)`), and paint() (pulse-shell.js:244) can prepend a `.hqp-note` error line directly above the first section in `.ps-body`.
critic.why: Sibling-to-sibling spacing is fine because the bottom margin carries it; the gap only vanishes where a section is the first child of something that is not `.ps-body`, or follows a non-section. It is the residual half of the auditors' finding, and the fix is the half they got right — but their proposed 1.5rem value would halve the shipped section gap.
critic.fix: Keep `--sp5`. Change :66 to `.hqp-sec { margin: var(--sp5) 0; }` and add `.ps-body > .hqp-sec:first-child, .hqp-area > .hqp-sec:first-child { margin-top: 0; }`. Adjacent margins collapse, so section-to-section stays 2.4rem and nothing else moves.

critic.title: THE ANALYST: it has no memory of anything it has ever published
critic.evidence: wrangler.toml declares `name`, `main`, `compatibility_date` and `[vars]` only — no KV, R2, D1, DO or `[triggers]`. index.js:39 `const rspCache = new Map(); // key -> {t, data}` is the only store, in-memory per isolate, 30 minutes (:586). evidence.js:427-435 reconstructs `daysRunning` by re-running `buildFacts(d, days.length - k)` for k = 1..3 over the SAME 8-day window. writer.js:89-92: "DO NOT LEAD WITH SOMETHING YOU LED WITH YESTERDAY … This is the single most important thing: he has been reading the same opening sentence for days and stopped believing the report."
critic.why: This is the root of Trym's complaint and the rewrite did not close it. `daysRunning` answers "was this fact also significant yesterday" — a proxy — not "did I lead with this yesterday", which is what the rule claims to enforce. The writer never sees its own previous headline, so it cannot vary its opening, cannot say "third morning running" in its own words, and cannot notice a trend it itself called two days ago. Worse, because the cache is per-isolate, two readers on the same morning can get two different Opus 5 reports and there is no record of which one Trym actually read.
critic.fix: Add one KV namespace to wrangler.toml (`[[kv_namespaces]] binding = "REPORTS"`). After a successful `writeReport` at index.js:686, `await env.REPORTS.put('report:' + yDate, JSON.stringify({headline: written.headline, verdict: written.verdict, shape: det.shape, leadIds: loud.slice(0,3).map(f => f.id)}), {expirationTtl: 60*60*24*30})`. Before calling the writer, read the last 7 keys and put them in the pack as `pack.previously = [{date, headline, leadIds}, …]`, with a prompt rule: "`previously` is what you published on earlier mornings. Do not reuse an opening you have already used, and if a fact appears in an earlier `leadIds`, it may appear only as a clause." Also read-through KV in apiAnalyst so a warm day never re-generates.

critic.title: THE ANALYST: the pack hands the model 19 finished sentences and never tells it not to quote them
critic.evidence: evidence.js:85-97 `const fact = (o) => ({ … say: o.say || null, because: o.because || null });` and every push supplies a complete grammatical sentence — e.g. :186-188 `say: … 'Traffic ' + moveWord(pS) + ' to ' + S + ' against a usual ' + Math.round(median(judgeAgainst)) + '.'`. buildPack ships them in `pack.facts` (:465). writer.js's SYSTEM (63-104) never mentions the word `say`, and rule 1 tells the model every figure it may use is already computed in the pack.
critic.why: Nineteen correct, grounded, pre-written English sentences are sitting in the prompt. The cheapest path for any model is to lightly reorder them — which reproduces exactly the "same each time with new numbers" feel the rewrite was built to end, only now it costs an Opus 5 call to produce. This is the single highest-leverage line in the whole analyst and no auditor read the new files.
critic.fix: Rename the field to `draft` in `fact()` and add rule 8 to SYSTEM: "Each fact carries `draft` — a sentence a template wrote for the fallback report. It is raw material and it is dull on purpose. Do not copy its phrasing or its sentence shape; use its numbers and say the thing your own way." If the report still reads templated after that, drop `draft` from the pack the writer sees entirely and pass only `label / value / unit / base / deltaPct / n / z / sig / daysRunning / because` — `narrate()` keeps its own copy for the deterministic path.

critic.title: THE ANALYST: a broken writer is invisible — the desk silently shows the report Trym complained about
critic.evidence: index.js:686-690 `if (written && !written.__err) { data = { ...data, ...written, by: 'written', shape: det.shape }; } else if (written && written.__err) { data.writerNote = written.__err;   // shown nowhere; read it in the payload }`. Neither the overlay (pulse-shell.js:286-298) nor the ledger card (hq-pulse.js:228-239) reads `an.by`, `an.written` or `an.writerNote`; `grep -rn "writerNote" src/` returns nothing.
critic.why: If the API key expires, the model id changes, the call times out, or the grounding check discards an invented number, Trym gets the deterministic report — the exact artefact he stopped believing — with no signal at all. He would conclude the rewrite did nothing. The one failure mode this system must never have silently, it has silently.
critic.fix: Render provenance under the verdict pill in both renderers. In pulse-shell.js after :286: `if (an.by !== 'written') el('div', 'hqp-cap', 'written by the rules' + (an.writerNote ? ' — the writer failed: ' + an.writerNote : ' — no writer key set'), card);` and `if (an.written) el('div', 'hqp-cap', 'written by ' + an.written, card);`. Mirror it in hq-pulse.js's googleBlock. It is two lines and it is the difference between a working feature and a feature that looks working.

critic.title: THE ANALYST: an Opus 5 call blocks the desk's own page load, on a cold isolate, non-streaming
critic.evidence: pulse-shell.js:372 `io.analyst().then((a) => { S.analyst = a; }).catch(() => {});` fires on mount, before the button is ever pressed. index.js:685 `const written = await writeReport(env, pack);` is awaited inline in the request. writer.js:156-169 posts non-streaming with `max_tokens: 16000` and no `output_config.effort`, so Opus 5 runs adaptive thinking at the default `high` effort. `rspCache` (index.js:39) is per-isolate with a 30-minute TTL (:586); wrangler.toml has no `[triggers]`.
critic.why: Every cold isolate that serves the Pulse tab pays a full Opus 5 judgement call synchronously, and Cloudflare's edge cuts a request at ~100s. The claude-api guidance is explicit that long or high-`max_tokens` requests should stream to avoid request timeouts. So the most likely production behaviour is a 524 on the very load that was supposed to fetch the report — falling through the `.catch(() => {})` to no analyst at all — and a variable Opus 5 bill driven by isolate churn rather than by days.
critic.fix: Move the write off the request path. Add `[triggers] crons = ["15 4 * * *"]` to wrangler.toml (after the Oslo day closes), do the `writeReport` in a `scheduled()` handler, and store the result in the same KV namespace as the memory fix. `/api/analyst` then reads KV and falls back to `analyse()` alone if the key is missing. That makes the cost exactly one Opus 5 call a day, removes the timeout entirely, and gives the persistence the daysRunning fix needs. Keep `max_tokens: 16000` non-streaming — inside a cron there is no HTTP deadline. Do NOT change the model id or the `output_config: { format: { type: 'json_schema', schema: SCHEMA } }` shape: both are current and correct.

critic.title: THE ANALYST: only four hard-coded pairs do the one job Trym asked for
critic.evidence: analyst.js:60-93 `crossFacts()` contains exactly four `if` blocks: traffic↓/engagement↑ (:66), traffic↑/engagement↓ (:73), sessions moved/downloads flat (:80), busy day/no checkout (:88). writer.js rule 5 (:94-97) asks the model for the same thing — "noticing that two numbers together mean something neither means alone" — but `buildPack` (evidence.js:442-468) ships no pairing candidates, only independent facts.
critic.why: "It doesn't feel valuable unless it actually gives good perspectives based on the different results each day" is a request for exactly this kind of sentence, and the deterministic path can produce four of them for the life of the product while the written path is asked for them with no grounded material to build one from — the model cannot compute a joint rate, because rule 1 forbids arithmetic.
critic.fix: Have evidence.js emit the pairs, not the prose. Add a `pairs` array to the pack: for every unordered pair of facts where both have a non-null `deltaPct` and `n >= MIN_STEP_N`, precompute `{a: idA, b: idB, aDelta, bDelta, sameDirection, jointN}` and keep the ten with the largest `|aDelta - bDelta|`. The model then has grounded numbers for a co-movement sentence and does not have to divide anything. Keep `crossFacts()` as-is for the fallback path — it is the deterministic report's only original writing.

critic.title: THE ANALYST: only two of the four statistical findings survive, and one of them is a one-word fix
critic.evidence: Still true: index.js:567 `body: JSON.stringify({ startDate: from, endDate: to, dataState: 'all', rowLimit: 1 })` — yesterday's fresh, incomplete GSC row is compared against a 7-day window fetched the same way at :665. Also still true: evidence.js:68-79 gates on constants (`Z_LOUD = 2.4`, `n < 8 || absDelta < 3`) rather than on a standard error. Already fixed and not to be re-patched: the level test is now three-part (`if (sep < 2.2 || p == null || Math.abs(p) < 40 || absGap < 25) return null;` at evidence.js:121), mean+sd became median+MAD (:32-45), and the offer zero-alarm now gates on `MIN_STEP_N` with the percentage behind `MIN_RATE_N` (:311-318).
critic.why: The stats lens cites analyst.js:180/259/266/343 in a 433-line file that is now 261 lines; applying those patches would edit code that no longer exists or re-fix what evidence.js already fixed correctly. The two live ones are worth doing and cheap.
critic.fix: Change `dataState: 'all'` to `dataState: 'final'` at index.js:567 — the catch at :669 already handles a missing search read gracefully, so the only cost is that search goes quiet for a day or two. For the sample gates, replace the constant `absDelta < 3` floor in `sigOf` with a proportion standard error where a rate is involved: `se = Math.sqrt(p*(1-p)/n + pBase*(1-pBase)/nBase)` and require `Math.abs(p - pBase) >= 1.96 * se`. Leave `robustZ`'s floor at :43 alone; it is correct and it is the reason the level check stopped firing daily.

critic.title: CONSISTENCY: which proposal wins where two lenses disagree
critic.evidence: Four live conflicts. (1) Spacing scale: `--s1…--s5` on `#bmPanePulse` vs the shipped `--sp1…--sp5` on `.bm-wrap` (:52-57), whose own comment at :47-51 says "THE SCALE HANGS ON .bm-wrap, NOT ON THE PANE'S ID … a margin of var(--sp5) with no --sp5 is a DROPPED DECLARATION". (2) Tables: the tables lens's new `.hqp-tbl.is-grid` + `.hqp-tn` vs the shipped `grid()` (hq-pulse.js:75) with `.hqp-grid/.hqp-gin/.hqp-grow/.hqp-gh/.hqp-gk/.hqp-gv`. (3) Ticker: `padding-left: 100%` + 34s + a 0.9rem mask (spacing) vs a 6%/94% mask (mobile) vs the shipped 35% + 26s + 3.5%/96.5% (:181-184). (4) GA4 budget: the coverage lens proposes four new runReports; index.js:606 says "The batch caps at FIVE requests and this is the fourth."
critic.why: Adopting both halves of any of these produces a third system rather than one. The scope conflict is the dangerous one: `#bmPanePulse` is exactly the trap the file documents, because the analyst overlay is mounted to `.bm-wrap` (pulse-shell.js:272), so pane-scoped tokens silently drop there.
critic.fix: (1) `.bm-wrap` and `--sp*` win — never re-scope to `#bmPanePulse`; extend `--sp*` if a step is missing, and hang `--lab`/`--key`/`--prose` there too. (2) `grid()` wins — it declares columns as data, already handles null→em dash and zero→quiet, and is already used three times; do not introduce `.hqp-tn`. (3) The shipped ticker wins on timing; take only the mask improvement, and make it a fixed gutter rather than a percentage: `linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0, #000 0.9rem, #000 calc(100% - 0.9rem), transparent 100%)`. (4) One GA4 slot, not four: spend it on the per-surface download series (it feeds the "Every surface…" panel Trym named); get the device split by adding `deviceCategory` to the existing daily report — but note index.js:625 `dayRow[dim(r, 0)] = r` keys by date alone and would silently keep only the last device per day, so it needs re-keying first. Everything else goes behind the pass and world service bindings, which cost no GA4 quota.

critic.title: THE ORDERED PLAN — one system, nothing done twice
critic.evidence: The dependency that fixes the ordering: every later change reads tokens declared on `.bm-wrap` (inbox.astro:52-63); the table migration deletes the classes the leader and zebra rules hang off (:211-240, :277-279); and the analyst's memory, cron and provenance changes all want the same KV namespace, so they are one commit, not three.
critic.why: Seven lenses produced seven patches against a stale tree. Sequenced this way each step's output is the next step's input, no rule is written twice, and the desk is verifiable as a player after every step.
critic.fix:
STEP 0 — Re-baseline. Diff all seven lenses against HEAD and strike everything already shipped (roughly half). Do not touch a line number any lens quotes without re-reading it.

STEP 1 — Finish the token system (one commit, inbox.astro:52-63). Add `--lab`, `--key`, `--prose`, `--prose-s`, `--ink-lab` beside `--num-*` on `.bm-wrap`. Nothing else changes yet.

STEP 2 — Spend the tokens (inbox.astro only). `.hqp-tk` :234, `.hqp-gk` :298, `.hqp-fname` :116 → label voice. Collapse the ~20 prose sizes onto `--prose`/`--prose-s`. Delete `opacity` from :85, :110, :330. `.hqp-cap` :95 loses its 0.2rem indent and gains a scoped bottom gap. `.hqp-sec` :66 gains a top margin with a `:first-child` reset. `.hqp-note` :72 gains a top margin with a `.hqp-h +` reset. Screenshot every room; this step alone answers most of Trym's paragraph.

STEP 3 — One table component. Migrate the six `.hqp-tbl` call sites (pulse-rooms.js:123, 144, 152, 248, 258, 418) to `grid()` with real headers, splitting the value-joins at :127 and :170 into their own columns as you go. Then delete `.hqp-trow`/`.hqp-tk`/`.hqp-tv`/`::after`/`is-head` (inbox.astro:211-240, 277-279) — which removes the empty-leader bug and the zebra-phase mismatch without either being fixed separately.

STEP 4 — The last two joins. Split `hqp-fnum` at pulse-rooms.js:449 and hq-pulse.js:204 onto a `.hqp-fsub` second line; split `hqp-abig` at pulse-rooms.js:414 into a value node and a `.hqp-alab` label node.

STEP 5 — Analyst infrastructure (one commit). Add `[[kv_namespaces]] REPORTS` and `[triggers] crons` to worker-pulse/wrangler.toml; move `writeReport` into a `scheduled()` handler; `/api/analyst` reads KV. This removes the page-load timeout AND creates the store the next step needs.

STEP 6 — Analyst memory and voice. Write `{headline, verdict, shape, leadIds}` to KV each morning; feed the last 7 back as `pack.previously`; rename `say` → `draft` and add the do-not-copy rule to SYSTEM; add the precomputed `pairs` array.

STEP 7 — Provenance. Render `an.by` / `an.written` / `an.writerNote` under the verdict pill in both renderers, so a broken writer can never again look like a working one.

STEP 8 — Coverage, one slot. `dataState: 'final'` at index.js:567, then the single free GA4 request on per-surface downloads.

STEP 9 — Mobile, last, at 393px. `.ps-rpt` sticky + a `.ps-bar` mask; 44px targets on `.hqp-i`, `.ps-chip`, `.ps-room`, `.ps-zbtn`; a fade affordance on `.hqp-grid`'s horizontal scroll. None of it is worth doing before the type and table systems settle, because all of it is measured against them.
